articleTitle: YOLO-DHC:A Multi-scale method for PCB defect detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: The stability of the equipment’s functioning may be impacted by surface flaws on the printed circuit board (PCB) caused by factors like the production environment. Aiming at the issues of small defect target, complex defect shape, missed detection and false detection in PCB surface defect detection, a YOLO-DHC surface defect detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv8 model is proposed. Firstly, the C2F-DC module based on dynamic convolution is proposed to replace the C2f module in the backbone network, which improves the feature extraction ability of the model by adaptive generation of convolutional kernel weights. Secondly, the HSD module is introduced to retain the details of defects in the process of downsampling. Finally, the CMSF multi-scale fusion module is presented to enhance the model’s detection capabilities even more. Compared with YOLOv8s, the experimental results show that the average accuracy (mAP) of the algorithm on the public PCB dataset is increased by 2.4%, and the recall rate is increased by 3.1%.

articleTitle: A Transformer Oil Temperature Anomaly Detection Method Based on LSTM-Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In response to the traditional detection methods have been difficult to effectively detect a large number of time-series oil temperature data and other problems. In this paper propose an unsupervised anomaly detection method that combines a long and short-term memory network (LSTM) with an Attention mechanism. Firstly, multiple LSTM units are formed into an LSTM network to collaborate with each other in order to learn the long-term dependencies of the data in the time series sequence. Subsequently, the Attention mechanism was introduced to automatically assign attention weights to the outputs of the LSTM units for each data point in a time series thereby performing weighted aggregation to obtain the predicted values. Finally, the oil temperature was evaluated whether it was anomalous or not based on the prediction error for each data in all the time series, and the experimental results showed that in comparison with the similar methods, both of them showed much better DBI (0.4477) and DVI (11.4516).

articleTitle: A two level cryptography scheme based on QR code and logistic mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Quick Response (QR) code, a two-dimensional graphic of square symbols, is widely applied due to its reliability, fast scanning, large data capacity and error correction. But its security has become a concern. From the perspective of information hiding, QR codes can transmit secret information. This paper presents a steganography scheme with two-layer information storage for protecting two secrets. The first layer uses the logistic mapping algorithm for the secret QR code image, and the second layer embeds another secret message into the QR code image via a reversible steganography algorithm. The contaminated transmission image doesn’t affect the extraction of the QR code image and the first layer of secret information. Even if the first layer’s hiding is broken, the second layer’s secret is unaffected. Combining QR code advantages and logistic chaotic mapping randomness, this scheme has low computational complexity, high interference robustness and large payload capacity. Theoretical analysis proves its effectiveness. Experimental results show it offers multiple encryption protection and decryption methods for two pieces of information and has many advantages over existing schemes.

articleTitle: Research on emergency response plan based on Internet of Things and image detection technology : Take the hijacking of the MTA public bus as an example
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: After the bus was hijacked, due to the closure of the internal place, the emergency management department was unable to understand the specific internal information and make accurate judgments in a timely manner, resulting in a broken link in the emergency rescue chain to obtain information. Taking MTA bus hijacking as an example, In this paper, an anomaly detection algorithm model for image data based on emergencies in specific scenes was proposed. Through the Internet of Things and image detection technology, it is possible to communicate information inside and outside the closed hostage site. This method can greatly improve the outside world’s grasp of the situation in the closed hijacking site, and “fill” a “broken link” in the “rescue chain” was not possible to know the inside of the hijacking site, fully supplement the information source of on-site decision-making in emergency management, and provide reference for emergency response and decision-making departments.

articleTitle: A Burst Topic Detection Model Based on HVCH Model and Burst_NBT Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This paper proposes a burst topic detection model based on HVCH model and Burst_NBT method. The model overcomes the sparsity difficulty of microblog by establishing HVCH model, effectively detects topics of microblog. Then the model establishes Burst_NBT method to calculate the burst scores of the words and cluster the burst words of microblog document sets of each topic, and to score and rank the burst word clusters to detect the corresponding burst topics of each topic. The experiment results indicate that the proposed HVCHBurst_NBT model improve the evaluation indicators compared with the other two burst topic detection models.

articleTitle: Predicting mooring system response using LDA-HBA-LSTM model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Accurate prediction of the response of mooring systems is essential to ensure the safety and reliability of offshore floating structures. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks have achieved promising results in time-series prediction tasks because of their excellent network architecture, but their performance is highly dependent on appropriate hyperparameter configurations. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Latin hypercube and density-assisted Honey Badger Algorithm Optimizer (LDA-HBA), which increases diversity by utilizing Latin hypercube sampling for population initialization, introduces density to enhance the strength formulation, and adaptive crossover operator to further improve the exploration capability of the algorithm and prevent it from falling into local optima. Experimental results show that the prediction accuracy of LDA-HBA-LSTM is better than the traditional model and converges faster.

articleTitle: A Distributed Task Allocation Algorithm for UAV Swarm Based on Local Information
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This article proposes a distributed task allocation algorithm based on local information for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm. A Part of the UAVs which are in the information exchange range participate in the local range auction. The auction members will change due to the movement of the UAVs in the following auctions. Each UAV in the swarm will be allocated a task by multiple rounds of local range auctions. The experimental data clearly demonstrate that the method has superior performance for enabling UAV swarm to complete the allocation of tasks based on local information.

articleTitle: Microservice Anomaly Monitoring Method based on Multi-dimensional Spatiotemporal Feature Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In a modern microservice architecture, the largescale distribution of services and high concurrency access make anomaly monitoring particularly complex. Traditional monitoring methods usually rely on a single data dimension, such as request delay or resource utilization, making capturing complex abnormal patterns challenging. Therefore, this paper proposes a microservice anomaly monitoring method based on multidimensional spatiotemporal feature reconstruction, aiming to reconstruct the complete feature space by integrating different data sources to improve the accuracy and robustness of anomaly detection. This paper’s method first extracts adequate data, such as service response time and service call chain from the tracking dataset, with time and space as the core and constructs it into a multi-dimensional feature matrix, fully considering the spatial and temporal correlation between microservices. Second, this paper introduces a deep learning model combining convolutional neural networks and gated recurrent cells to capture dynamic dependence and feature interactions in spatiotemporal dimensions. The convolutional neural network module extracts the spatial dependence through the convolution operation, while the gating cycle unit module captures the changing trend of the time series. By paralleling two modules and introducing the attention mechanism, the model is optimized with the reconstruction error, and finally, the network abnormality is judged by setting the threshold.

articleTitle: Research on Traffic Police Area Target Detection and Dynamic Tracking Based on YOLOv8 and Optical Flow Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning technologies in the field of autonomous driving, significant progress has been made in traffic police gesture detection and recognition. However, traffic police area detection still faces certain challenges and requires further optimization and innovation. To address issues such as low accuracy and poor robustness in dynamic traffic police area recognition, this paper designs a traffic police area tracking system tailored to the demands of real-world traffic scenarios. In urban road conditions, YOLOv8 is used for detecting the traffic police area, and corner detection algorithms from optical flow methods are employed for position tracking, improving the system’s effectiveness in traffic environments.

articleTitle: Research on Global Path Planning of Unmanned Ground Vehicles in Off-Road Environments Based on Improved A* Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In off-road environments, where road information is unclear, terrain is very rugged, and the boundaries between passable and impassable areas are indistinct, paths planned by traditional algorithms tend to result in low lateral driving stability and high energy consumption. To address these problems, this research proposes improvements to the environmental modeling approach and cost function of the traditional $\mathrm{A}^{*}$ algorithm, aiming to generate paths that consider distance, energy consumption, and lateral driving stability. Firstly, slope calculations are applied to the initial Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data to create a vehicle-passable map based on the vehicle’s maximum pitch angle, maximum rollover angle, and manually designated obstacle regions. Secondly, vehicle pitch and rollover angle factors are incorporated into the cost function of the traditional $\mathrm{A}^{*}$ algorithm. Finally, the simulation results on maps of different sizes show that compared with the traditional A* algorithm, the path planned by the algorithm in this research is able to reduce energy consumption and improve the stability of the vehicle’s lateral travel in off-road environments, with less increase in the path distance.

articleTitle: Safety Helmet Detection System Based on YOLOv5 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: As a major infrastructure powerhouse, ensuring the safety of construction workers in China is crucial. Construction site accidents are mainly caused by harsh working environments, improper operations by workers, and inadequate supervision by managers. Among these, wearing a safety helmet properly can significantly reduce the consequences of accidents. Currently, checking whether workers are wearing safety helmets on construction sites is primarily done manually, a method that is time-consuming and inefficient. With the development of object detection technologies, deep learning-based methods have gradually become the focus of research. Therefore, this paper takes the YOLOv5s algorithm as the technical foundation to design and implement a real-time safety helmet detection system.

articleTitle: High proportion of hydropower dominates the grid spot market clearing model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In the context of dual-carbon targets and power market reform, promoting the consumption of hydropower-based renewable energy through market-based mechanisms has become a key task in the construction of China’s electricity spot market. Including hydropower in the design of market clearing mechanism, taking into account the operational characteristics of hydropower, introducing complex constraints such as hydraulic coupling, power generation characteristics, water level control and so on into the conventional clearing model, and based on the IEEE30 node system, designing the day-ahead market example consisting of six power generating main bodies, and initially verifying the reasonableness and practicality of the proposed clearing model by analysing the results of the market transactions in different operational scenarios. By analysing the market trading results under different operation scenarios, the rationality and practicality of the proposed clearing model are initially verified.

articleTitle: GLoM-PCNet: A Deep Network for Multi-scale Information Fusion for Point Cloud Completion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Point cloud completion is a pivotal task within point cloud analysis, with the objective of transforming incomplete and sparse point clouds into their dense and complete 3D shape. Conventional methods often falter in effectively harnessing and synthesizing multi-scale, global, and local information during the reconstruction process. To surmount these hurdles, we propose GLoM-PCNet, a transformer-based framework to efficiently extract and amalgamate global and local multi-scale information for point cloud completion. This framework processes the input point cloud by employing a trilayered self-attention mechanism across different scales, which fosters dynamic interactions with global information and ensures the proficient fusion of multi-scale data. Furthermore, we innovate a k-nearest neighbor knn-based local multi-scale perception technique that significantly enhances the representation of local detail features through multi-scale integration. The harmonious fusion of multi-scale features at both global and local levels empowers GLoM-PCNet to achieve exceptional performance across a spectrum of benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: An efficient hybrid uncertainty propagation method for structures based on polynomial chaos kriging
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In complex mechanical systems, intricate uncertainty factors often exist, which can significantly impact the key performance and reliability of the system. Conducting propagation analysis of these complex uncertainties is a crucial approach for assessing the stability and safety of structural performance. However, traditional uncertainty propagation analysis methods may encounter a series of challenges, such as difficulties in model construction and time-consuming solutions, particularly when addressing the analysis of complex mechanical systems that involve various hybrid uncertainty factors. In response to these challenges, this study proposes a propagation analysis method for mechanical structures with hybrid uncertainties based on Polynomial Chaos Kriging (PCK). This method constructs a fundamental model for the black-box problems of complex equipment using PCK and incorporates Gegenbauer polynomials during the modeling process to enhance the adaptability of PCK in the presence of complex uncertain variables. Furthermore, this research introduces targeted sampling techniques for PCK modeling under hybrid uncertainty to maximize the efficiency of sample utilization. The analytical efficiency and solution accuracy of the proposed algorithm are validated through one numerical example and one engineering example of a drive axle shell analysis.

articleTitle: Research on Steel Production Scheduling Optimization based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Steel production scheduling represents a pivotal aspect of the steel manufacturing process, encompassing the strategic allocation of resources and the optimization of production processes. This directly impacts the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the production process. However, conventional scheduling optimization techniques are ill-equipped to address the intricate nuances of the steel production environment and the deluge of real-time data. In this work, a method of steel production scheduling optimization based on deep reinforcement learning was proposed and subsequently innovated and optimized. The Deep Q Network (DQN) was employed as the fundamental model, with the objective of enhancing the stability and convergence speed of the model. This was achieved through the design of the state space and action space of production scheduling, as well as the incorporation of experience playback and target networks. With regard to model optimization, an adaptive adjustment mechanism of the reward function is proposed, which enables the model to balance the optimization of multiple objectives, such as production efficiency and energy consumption, with greater accuracy. Furthermore, the network structure has been enhanced and a multi-head attention mechanism has been incorporated to augment the model’s capacity for scheduling decisions in intricate production scenarios. The optimized model was subjected to experimental verification on an actual steel production dataset, and its performance in terms of scheduling efficiency and resource allocation accuracy was found to be excellent.

articleTitle: Clock Domain Crossing Aware RTL Synthesis using Fusion Compiler in Commercial Display Chip Design
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: As the performance requirements of display chips increase, less area, less power consumption, good performance display chip become more critical factors for LCD panel manufacturer. So this puts a lot of demands on chip development. Chip designer need speed up the chip development iteration rate. There are many methods to achieve this goal by the way introduce new problem. For example, to get better performance design house will use same RTL code do process transfer. But same RTL may not suitable in timing aspect for difference design process. RTL designer use high level Synthesis tool create RTL more fastly. Some company may purchase soft encrypted RTL IP from IP vendor. But high level synthesis rtl & encrypted rtl make RTL design unreadable. It increase clock domain crossing risk during design optimization. These give more challenge for design synthesis & implementation engineer. Fusion Compile (FC) is an EDA tool from Synopsys. It combined synthesis stage and place route. Make implementation step more efficiency. More compact implementation method speed up design cycle. More ever It make design timing closure more easily and get good power area. Design house can use this tool achieve difficult design goal. We present a fusion compile design flow. To solve clock domain crossing issue in implementation design stage and apply this flow for one of arithmetic block in commercial display chip. Get good optimize results avoid any clock domain crossing risk.

articleTitle: Research on Concealed Dangerous Goods Detection Based on Active Terahertz Active Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Active Terahertz imaging technology exhibits significant potential in security inspection due to its advantages of rapid imaging, strong penetration capabilities, and harmlessness to humans. It is poised to become a mainstream technology in this field. However, the study of detecting concealed dangerous goods in terahertz human imaging using deep learning remains in its infancy, facing challenges such as limited databases, low image resolution and contrast, and inadequate small-object detection capabilities. This paper addresses these challenges by introducing a large-scale dataset with over $\mathbf{1 2, 0 0 0}$ terahertz images from the TGR-23 system, covering 10 categories of hazardous items, and enhancing small-object detection through the improvement of the YOLOv8 model by incorporating a Context Feature Extension Module (CAM) and a Residual Improved CAM (RCAM), which resulted in a 2% increase in detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on the Design Methodology and Performance Analysis of a Combined Robot within the Context of ROBOTAC Competition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This paper designs and manufactures a combined robot for the ROBOTAC competition based on mechanical principles and control principles. The robot consists of a base robot and a biomimetic crawling robot. It adopts direct current motors to drive mecanum wheels for rapid movement, and the launching device uses pneumatic components. Through the analysis and calculation of the state equations of each chamber of the cylinder, the piston motion equation, etc., relevant parameters are determined, and a mechanical structure equipped with a lifting coupling mechanism, a locking mechanism and a fire-kindling launching mechanism is designed. The hardware adopts a modular design, with the Infineon automotive-grade single-chip microcomputer TC297 as the main control unit, and the $\mathbf{C}$ language programming is used to realize the control function. In the competition, the success rate of the robot in retrieving firekindlings reached 100%. Cooperating with other robots, it won the second prize in the national competition, which verified the effectiveness of the design and provided a reference example for the teaching of robot-related majors in colleges and universities and the cultivation of innovative talents.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of a Six-Degree-of-Freedom Passive Vibration Isolation System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Passive vibration isolation systems are widely employed in high-precision instruments to ensure the stability of their operational environment. First, a theoretical model of the six-degree-of-freedom passive vibration isolation system is established based on the principles of rigid body dynamics. The modal decoupling of the free vibrations in the six-degree-offreedom system is analyzed, and MATLAB simulations are conducted to obtain the six mode shapes and the time-domain response of the displacement for each of the six degrees of freedom. Secondly, the dynamic characteristics of the passive vibration isolation system are analyzed under various key parameters, providing a theoretical basis for the design and optimization of active vibration control.

articleTitle: MS-BEV: Multi-Scales Transformer for Object Enhanced 3D Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Perceptual tasks are crucial in the field of autonomous driving and robot applications. At present, BEV perception algorithm plays a major role in multi view 3D object detection. Because of its intuitive expression and easier fusion, there are still some problems. In recent years, by adding timing fusion to make up for the limitations of single needle sensing, the accuracy and continuity of the sensing algorithm have been improved. In order to solve the problem of information loss in the process of time series fusion, this paper proposes a transform based network MS-BEV. By combining the time characteristics of time fusion and object enhancement mechanism, it enhances the understanding of dynamic object movement and solves the Long-Distance problem. Firstly, we implement a decoder layer that integrates the camera intrinsics and supports multi-scale processing, by leveraging the geometric properties of visual images. Then, we designed an object centered guided aggregation decoder to accelerate model convergence. Finally, we utilize the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) to achieve the feature alignment and fusion of objects. We conduct extensive experiments on the nuScenes dataset to validate the merits of our proposed MS-BEV.

articleTitle: Intelligent hydrogen flame recognition method: Comparisons among SVM, GA-SVM and PSO-SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In this paper, the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization are used to obtain the kernel parameters of the radial basis function of the Support Vector Machine (SVM), and the optimized SVM algorithm is used to realize intelligent identification of hydrogen flame. The feasibility of this method is a crucial aspect that assures its practicality. Dual-band $(1.9 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ and $2.7 \mu \mathrm{~m}$) infrared sensors are used to collect hydrogen flame data in the special infrared band. The hydrogen flame data is used to extract its time-domain and frequent-domain characteristics, including the average voltage value of the hydrogen flame time-domain data and the frequency corresponding to the maximum frequency amplitude and maximum amplitude of the frequency domain data. The above feature data is used as the algorithm input. The classification accuracy of the training set, test set, optimization time, and error fitness curve are taken as the evaluation indexes of the algorithm, and the complex hydrogen flame identification problem is transformed into a binary classification problem with faster speed, higher efficiency, and higher accuracy by support vector machine algorithm. The experimental results show that the PSO-SVM has the highest accuracy on hydrogen flame, and SVM has the shortest optimization time. GA-SVM has the longest optimization time, and its accuracy is lower than that of PSOSVM. Moreover, the recognition accuracy of the PSO-SVM training set and the test set are ${9 9 \%}$ and ${1 0 0 \%}$, respectively, and its optimization time does not exceed 2 s. The recognition effect is better than that of the traditional support vector machine, and a genetic algorithm optimizes the support vector machine, which means that the hydrogen flame identification and detection method based on the SVM algorithm is feasible, and the particle swarm optimization can obtain better recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: A Gain and Slew Rate Enhanced Recycling Folded Cascode Operational Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: An improved folded cascode operational amplifier with current-recycling architecture has been proposed. This operational amplifier employs a current-multiplying architecture, with an added output stage to enhance gain. Additionally, a dynamic control unit has been integrated to improve the circuit’s slew rate. Designed and validated using a $0.18 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ CMOS process, simulation results indicate that the low-frequency gain of the proposed amplifier is 93.12 dB, with a gain-bandwidth product (GBW) of 2.6 MHz and an average slew rate of $26.97 \mathrm{MV} / \mathrm{s}$. Compared to the traditional structure, the gain has been increased by a factor of 9, and the slew rate has been enhanced by a factor of 21.

articleTitle: Thickness Distribution Prediction of Superplastic Forming Parts Based on Machine Learning and Computer Aided Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In recent years, the high-speed and high-performance needs of aircraft put forward higher requirements for superplastic forming process, in which uneven thickness distribution is one of the important factors affecting the performance of formed parts, and it increases the cost of design and manufacturing. Therefore, this study proposes using neural networks to predict the thickness distribution of superplastic formed parts. We established BP neural network and PSO-BP neural network to predict the thickness distribution of cross-section edges of box-shaped parts. The prediction performance of the two models is compared and the results show that the PSO-BP neural network has a higher prediction accuracy, especially in the area of the round corners. It is demonstrated that the method is feasible and significantly improves the computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Finite-time Sliding Mode Control Method for a Class of Air Intake Testing Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel finite-time sliding mode control method for the enhancement of the velocity and precision in the control of temperature and pressure within a class of air intake testing devices. Initially, a simulation model of the device without heat transfer characteristics is constructed in MATLAB, followed by the design of a sliding mode control strategy for the device. Then an auxiliary function characterized by a normal distribution is introduced, facilitating the formulation of a novel finite-time reaching law and an integral sliding mode surface, and culminating in the derivation of a finite-time sliding mode controller. Employing the Lyapunov stability theorem, it is demonstrated that the system state attains its equilibrium point within a finite time. Finally, three different reaching laws are used with the proposed sliding mode surface to construct the three controllers. Simulation experiments are conducted in the simulation model using the aforementioned three sliding mode controllers. The simulation results indicate that the sliding mode controller under the influence of the reaching laws presented in this paper significantly enhances the servo tracking performance of temperature and pressure.

articleTitle: Design of the control system of the harvester threshing drum
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In the context of modern agricultural development, the pursuit of enhanced efficiency and reliability in harvesting machinery has become a crucial focus. In this study, an innovative harvester threshing drum control system was proposed with the overarching aim of optimizing operational efficiency and substantially reducing the failure rate of the threshing drum. The design philosophy underpinning this system emphasizes intelligence and modernity, with the driving speed being identified as the principal adjustment parameter. By conducting rigorous verification of the fuzzy PID algorithm and in-depth analysis of experimental results, it was conclusively confirmed that the system exerts a significant and precise control effect on the rotational speed of the threshing drum. The experimental outcomes unequivocally demonstrate that the fuzzy PID controller exhibits rapid response capabilities and outstanding dynamic performance even when subjected to external interferences. This not only offers a practical and feasible pathway for the advancement of intelligent harvesters but also holds great significance for the continuous improvement of agricultural mechanization, potentially revolutionizing the way harvesting operations are carried out in the field.

articleTitle: An Improved SlowFast Model for Violence Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: As social safety concerns become increasingly prominent, the importance of violence detection has become increasingly significant. Accurately identifying violent behavior helps facilitate timely interventions, reducing harm and losses, thereby enhancing public safety. To minimize the interference from irrelevant actions (e.g., those from spectators and uninvolved individuals) during violence detection, this study proposes an improved SlowFast method that enhances the robustness of the model by modifying the network structure of the Slow Pathway and lateral connections. In the Slow Pathway, the original residual block is replaced with an SE-Res residual block, which strengthens the weighting of channel importance, making the model more stable in complex scenarios. The lateral connections are improved by integrating a 3D-Convolutional Block Attention Module (3D-CBAM), enhancing feature fusion and increasing the model’s sensitivity to key features across different temporal scales. Furthermore, to address the class imbalance issue within the dataset, the Focal Loss function has been modified, effectively improving the performance of each class. The improved model demonstrates excellent performance in violence detection tasks, achieving an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 6. 6 7 \%}$, which is a $\mathbf{1. 1 2 \%}$ improvement over the classical model.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Optimization Approach Using Rounding-Off Particle Swarm Optimization for the Crowdsourced Resource Scheduling Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: An application of the scheduling problem for projects with multiskill resource limits is the Crowdsourcing Resource Scheduling Problem (CRSP). Since the crowdsourcing issue with resource scheduling also involves resource constraints and skill matching problems, it is consistent with the core principles of Muti-skill Resource Constrained project Scheduling Problem (MS-RCPSP). Therefore, a two-stage optimization method (TS-RND-PSO) based on rounding-off particle swarm optimization (RND-PSO) was proposed to model the CRSP model by using MS-RCPSP framework. To begin, the task sequence vector is utilized to encode the solution, and a decoding technique incorporating resource limitations and talent matching is presented to provide a realistic scheduling scheme. Then, the twostage dynamic inertia weight adjustment strategy is adopted to expand the search area and enhance the widespread search ability by optimizing the high inertia weight in the early stage, to avoid falling into the local optimal. In the second stage, the inertia weight is gradually reduced, and the search area is aggregated to the local area near the optimal solution to increase the algorithm’s comprehension accuracy and convergence efficiency. Results from experiments indicate that when compared to conventional techniques, the proposed algorithm has significant advantages in scheduling accuracy and convergence speed.

articleTitle: Hypergraph-Based Network for Accurate Concrete Bridge Surface Damage Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This study addresses the issues of insufficient semantic information representation and weak higher-order feature relationships in the instance segmentation of concrete bridge surface damages. We propose an improved YOLO 11 model framework, which combines the CBAM attention module and HyperC2Net (Hypergraph-Based Cross-Level and Cross-Position Representation Network) to enhance feature extraction and semantic information modeling, significantly improving the damage detection and segmentation performance. The experiments are conducted on a concrete bridge surface damage dataset containing four common types of damage: cracks, spall, rebar, and corrosion. The performance of the proposed method is compared with existing YOLO models using various evaluation metrics such as mAP50, mAP50-95. The experimental results show that the proposed method improves 2.2% in accuracy over the existing YOLO model.

articleTitle: Priority-aware Log Collection Method for Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Effective troubleshooting of product system issues is vital for both customers and system providers. The primary role of a system log is to document system states and significant events at various critical junctures, aiding in the debugging of system failures and facilitating root cause analysis. While much research focuses on automated log analysis, there is limited research on efficient $\log$ collection. This paper introduces a priority-aware log collection method for storage systems. This method intelligently adjusts the log execution order based on the storage system’s actual Configuration Operation, Health Audit, and Dependency Relationship, ensuring that the key logs and diagnostic information of higher-priority components are collected first. This method is beneficial and significant in promptly addressing and resolving product issues.

articleTitle: Automated Red Circle Badge Detection and Clearing for Enhanced Mobile User Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of smartphones, red circle badges have become a common visual cue used by mobile applications to notify users of new notifications. While effective in driving user engagement, accumulating these red circles can lead to information overload and user stress. This paper presents a novel solution to automatically clear red circle badges to reduce user stress and improve the mobile user experience. The proposed approach includes two methods: YOLOv7-based model training for detecting red circle badges and a depth-first traversal algorithm for clearing them. Using a dataset of 126 screenshots containing 390 red circle badges, experimental results demonstrate the model achieves high accuracy in detection, with a recall of 98% and a precision of 92%, confirming its robustness. Additionally, experiments conducted on 10 apps show that the red circle badge clearing algorithm performs excellently in terms of efficiency, with an average processing time of 5.9 seconds per badge.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation Based on the Automated Testing Technology for Mass-produced Aerospace Products
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In this paper, automated testing technology was comprehensively investigated to address the challenges remaining in traditional manual testing of mass-produced aerospace products. The software portion of the testing system was developed upon the foundation of the original testing system. Subsequently, in combination with hardware interface devices, the automated testing technology for pulse loads was incorporated into the testing system, substituting the traditional manual testing methods. Ultimately, fully automated and intelligent testing of mass-produced aerospace products was achieved, which enhanced the testing efficiency and eliminated potential risks resulting from human operations. For massproduced aerospace products, this effectively saved time costs, ensured product production progress and quality control, and improved the reliability and safety of the testing system.

articleTitle: A High-capacity Information Hiding Scheme Based on Blakley Secret Sharing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: A high-capacity reversible information hiding scheme based on Blakley secret sharing is proposed to address the issues of low embedding rate and weak disaster recovery performance of images when using reversible information hiding to protect data in scenarios with large data transmission. The scheme employs Euclidean division and a two-dimensional modulus function to establish a robust mapping relationship between the secret information and the pixels of the cover image. Subsequently, the values derived from the preprocessing of the secret information are incorporated into the secret sharing method proposed by Blakley as the elements of the secret vector. The proposed scheme exploits the disaster-tolerance property of the secret sharing method and enhances the redundancy of the secret-carrying encrypted image, thereby improving the embedding rate and security of the algorithm while maintaining the security of the secret sharing.

articleTitle: Adjustable multidimensional environment monitoring system connected to the cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the rapid development of industrialization and urbanization, environmental pollution and indoor air quality problems are becoming increasingly serious, and the demand for environmental monitoring technology is also growing. The rapid development of IoT technology has provided new solutions for environmental monitoring. Based on the above background, this system provides an integrated environmental monitoring solution, which monitors the temperature, humidity, light intensity, CO concentration, alcohol gas concentration, and smoke concentration of the environment through the STM32H7 microcontroller and Tencent Cloud server interconnection, providing users with accurate and timely environmental information to ensure public health and safe production. The system mainly uses MQ2, MQ7, DHT11, photosensitive and other modules to monitor multidimensional environments in real time, and displays the currently measured parameters on the system monitor. At the same time, through the Guanghetong L610 (GL610) communication module equipped with Qualcomm Snapdragon X55 chip, the system can synchronously upload measurement data to the cloud, achieving interconnection between monitoring systems and mobile applications. The user can adjust the threshold value of each parameter on the application side. Once the measured data of the system exceed the threshold value set by the user, the system will automatically send an alert to remind the user through WeChat official account push and call. The experimental results show that the system has advantages such as high-precision detection, real-time data transmission, intelligent warning, remote control, and data visualization.

articleTitle: A Pre-Sorted Autoencoder-based Prediction for Dynamic Multiobjective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In this paper, a pre-sorted autoencoder-based prediction algorithm, named PSAE, was proposed to solve dynamic multiobjective optimization problems (DMOPs). Since transfer learning enables knowledge acquisition from related tasks, its application to predict the Pareto-optimal solutions has gained increasing attention. Especially, the autoencoder (AE) was introduced to solve DMOPs and has gained promising results. However, the current AE-based prediction lacks an effective mechanism to match input and output knowledge, leading to inconsistencies between the input and output solutions. For solving this problem, for the first time, the thin-plate spline robust point matching (TPS-RPM) method is introduced to achieve knowledge matching between inputs and outputs, thus enhancing prediction accuracy. To verify the effectiveness of proposed algorithm, some recently proposed dynamic multiobjective evolutionary algorithms are selected in the experiments and the results show the superiority of PSAE.

articleTitle: A Code Comment Generation Method Based on Information Retrieval and Code Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Code comments can help developers quickly understand code and reduce maintenance costs. However, due to the widespread phenomenon of code cloning and the complex syntax structure of code, existing comment generation methods, which rely solely on Syntax Tree (AST) representations of code information, often result in low-quality comments. Therefore, this paper proposes a code comment generation method based on information retrieval and code structural information. By leveraging information retrieval techniques that combine code semantics, syntax, and lexical features, the method retrieves the most similar results from a codebase and integrates abstract syntax trees with data flow graphs to further improve the accuracy of comment generation. Experimental results show that, compared to mainstream methods, this approach achieves better performance on Python datasets, and the generated comments exhibit higher readability.

articleTitle: Dual-Dimensional Self-Attention for Facial Attribute Editing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Currently, methods based on the Enhanced Vision Transformer with Dual-Dimensional Self-Attention effectively capture long-range dependencies in images by computing self-attention mechanisms across multiple dimensions. This approach demonstrates superior performance in tasks such as image classification and object detection by partitioning images into small patches and treating them as sequential data. In this paper, we propose a framework that utilizes Dual-Dimensional Self-Attention as an encoder for image inversion. Unlike the complex model structure of encoder4editing, we employ a single modular component and use a simple network to reconstruct and edit real images. Experimental results indicate that this method excels in high-quality image inversion, with only a slight reduction in editing accuracy. Its reconstruction and editing performance are both slightly better than the complex structure based on encoder4editing.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Aircraft Engines Based on Multi-Scale Temporal Convolution and Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: The Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction of aircraft engines is a key component of intelligent maintenance strategies, as it can effectively prevent sudden failures, optimize maintenance schedules, and reduce maintenance costs. However, RUL prediction is challenged by noise, outliers in sensor data, and the complexity of modeling diverse operating conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes an RUL prediction framework for the C-MAPSS multivariate time series dataset. The framework first enhances input data quality by designing an efficient data cleaning method based on Kalman filtering and outlier detection. Next, a multi-scale temporal convolution module is introduced to capture both short-term fluctuations and long-term trend features, and sequence and time attention mechanisms are incorporated to improve the model’s ability to capture key features. Finally, the framework’s effectiveness is validated through model comparisons and ablation experiments.

articleTitle: Integrating Multiple Anomaly Assumptions: An Out-of-Distribution Detection Method in Driving Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Deep learning models struggle to recognize objects they have never encountered, often confidently classifying them as known classes. This can pose risks in certain application scenarios. A solution to this challenge is out-of-distribution (OoD) detection, which can identify objects that do not belong to known classes. However, existing methods typically rely on a single anomaly metric, leading to insufficient modeling of the original data. To address this, this paper proposes a novel anomaly metric that integrates different anomaly assumptions, enabling more reliable detection of out-of-distribution data without incurring additional computational costs. Additionally, we introduce a new loss function to optimize this metric and mitigate the issue of model overconfidence. The proposed method has been extensively tested on two driving scenario benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: CRALA: A Chinese-centric Risk Simulation and Assessment Framework for LLM Agents
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In recent years, large language models (LLMs) become more and more powerful. They can do many interesting tasks, like connecting to different external tools—sometimes we call them “plugins”—to help handle real things in the world. But at the same time, giving LLM agents more real-world power also creates a lot of risks we must be careful about. Checking these risks is not easy at all. It can cost lots of time and energy because we have to make special plugins and do complicated tests just to see if the model might do something unsafe. Most of the “serious” security checks, like the ones done on GPT-4, focus mostly on English. In Chinese, we know very little about the dangers with existing research. Many research pays attention to English, but not so much to Chinese cases, even though it’s super important. To fix this problem, we made a new framework called CRALA (Chinese-centric Risk Assessment for LLM Agents). It can simulate many situations in Chinese and then carefully check if there are any safety issues hiding inside these LLM agent tasks. CRALA includes two main parts: a Chinese Interaction Simulator, which creates and records pretend conversations, and an Evaluator, which looks at all these interactions and decides if interaction might be unsafe. We tested CRALA with human reviewers on 55 different Chinese scenarios. The results show that about $\mathbf{8 1. 5 \%}$ collected test cases are realistic. When the CRALA flags a case as dangerous, about 63.5% really were problems. We even tested 100 risky cases in Chinese apps with popular LLMs like GPT-4. GPT-4 only handled around 35% of them safely. This shows that we still have a long way to go before we can trust these agents completely, at least in Chinese contexts. In conclusion, CRALA makes checking these risks much less painful and gives us a better understanding of how safe Chinese LLM agents really are.

articleTitle: Enhancing Security with Intelligent Video Surveillance: An In-Depth Study of Technology, Applications, and System Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the continuous progress of science and technology and the acceleration of urbanization, the application of security monitoring systems in public safety, commercial monitoring and home security has become increasingly important. However, the current traditional monitoring system has many limitations in terms of function and performance. The traditional monitoring system mainly relies on human monitoring, which is not only inefficient, but also prone to missing and false alarms. In addition, these systems often lack intelligent processing capabilities to identify and respond to potential threats in a timely and accurate manner. The intelligent video surveillance system uses advanced image processing and artificial intelligence technology to automatically analyze video content, detect and identify abnormal behavior in real time, and greatly improve the efficiency and security of monitoring. The advantage of intelligent video surveillance system is that it can provide automatic alarm and response functions, reduce human intervention, and improve the comprehensiveness and timeliness of security protection. The goal of this research is to further improve the security and monitoring efficiency through the application of intelligent video surveillance technology, and realize automatic alarm and response systems. The study will focus on the specific application of intelligent video surveillance in multiple application scenarios such as urban security, commercial surveillance, and home security, as well as the key components required by the system, including cameras, analysis servers, and user interfaces. Through the in-depth research and application of intelligent video surveillance technology, it is expected to provide more intelligent and efficient solutions for various security monitoring needs.

articleTitle: Design of Second-order Reconfigurable Negative Group Delay Circuit Based on Split Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: A second-order reconfigurable negative group delay circuit based on the split ring resonator (SRR)is proposed in this paper, which achieves the reconfigurability of the center frequency and negative group delay peak value of the circuit by loading different capacitors and resistors. The circuit is designed to expand the bandwidth and improve the frequency response range by utilizing two series-connected SRR. At the same time, a matching circuit is loaded on the transmission line to optimize the return loss, thereby increasing the energy utilization efficiency of the circuit. Finally, the operating frequency range of the negative group delay circuit of the proposed circuit was controlled within 1.752GHz to 2.112GHz, with peak values of negative group delay range from 1.159ns to 4.496ns.

articleTitle: Workspace Simulation of a Dual-arm Work Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In complex operational tasks, the utilization rate of the dual-arm aerial manipulator is significantly better than that of the single robotic arm, which enables it to adapt to a wider range of operational tasks. The range of motion of the end effector of the dual arm aerial manipulator directly determines the workspace of the aerial manipulator, and its size is an important indicator for measuring the performance of the dual arm robot. The workspace is the collection of all positions and postures reachable by the end effector. Kinematic modeling is carried out for the robot arm, and based on this model, the workspace simulation is carried out for the end of the robot arm, and the simulation results verify the feasibility and validity of the design of the dual-arm work robot system.

articleTitle: Research on an improved MOTR-GRU multi-target tracking and behavior analysis method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Localizing people and identifying their behaviors in videos is a challenging task in advanced video understanding. However, traditional behavior recognition algorithms only detect the behavior of a single target and use a two-stage method for feature extraction and behavior recognition, which leads to problems such as difficulty in distinguishing individual behaviors and low recognition accuracy. To address these problems, an end-to-end multi-target human tracking and behavior analysis method, MOTR-GRU, is proposed to solve the problems of difficulty in distinguishing individual behaviors and low accuracy caused by accumulated errors in multi-target tracking and behavior analysis. First, the model continuously tracks different human targets in the video by extending the detection query in MOTR as the tracking query, and obtains relatively accurate tracking results without post-processing. Then, the gating mechanism is used to process and fuse the human information captured by the tracking module, enhance the model’s ability to process time series data, and analyze the behaviors of multiple targets frame by frame. Finally, the focal loss is used to reduce the impact of target category imbalance. Experiments are carried out on the Volleyball dataset. The results show that the behavior recognition accuracy of the end-to-end MOTR-GRU method reaches $\mathbf{6 8. 6 \%}$. This shows that the MOTR-GRU method can improve the ability of multi-target behavior analysis while ensuring the real-time tracking of targets.

articleTitle: Research on passive location algorithm of UAV based on TDOA
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In the airport environment, foreign body debris (FOD) can seriously damage the aircraft engine and harm human health, but the traditional method can not detect foreign body accurately and timely. Based on this, this paper proposes a method based on improved YOLOv8 to detect FOD. To solve the problem of slow detection of the original model, FasterBlock module is introduced in the backbone network to replace C2f module in the original network to speed up the model calculation. Aiming at the problem of low detection accuracy, DilateFormer module is introduced to realize multi-scale sensing. Furthermore, the loss function is modified to further improve the detection accuracy. The experiment on the airport runway foreign body detection data set shows that the improved algorithm mAP50 is 95.5%, which is 4 percentage points higher than the improved algorithm. The newly designed algorithm has a good application prospect in FOD detection with low model complexity and high detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on multi-objective control torque distribution strategy for distributed drive vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Aiming at the characteristic of individually controllable torque of distributed-drive electric vehicles, based on vehicle stability control and motor energy consumption optimization as well as considering the tire adhesion stability margin of the wheels, a multi-objective optimization function is established and weight coefficients for coordinating the stability control objective and the economy control objective are designed, and the dynamic weight coefficients are solved by means of the $\beta$ $\dot{\beta}$ phase plane plot with the aim of improving the vehicle operation stability and motor energy efficiency. Among them, the upper layer controller calculates the additional swing torque and designs a PI vehicle speed tracking controller through a sliding film controller. In the lower layer control, the vehicle traveling state is judged by $\boldsymbol{\beta}-\dot{\boldsymbol{\beta}}$ phase diagram and the multi-objective function weight coefficients are adjusted in real time accordingly. The advantages and disadvantages of the proposed strategy are verified by Simulink and Carsim joint simulation experiments, under DLC and Sine conditions, compared with the average distribution strategy, the vehicle is well stabilized under the coordinated multi-objective control and the energy saving is improved by a large increase in energy utilization by 7.4% and 12.3%. The research results help to improve the overall performance of distributed drive.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Systems Field Strength Prediction for High-Speed Maglev Train Based on STAR
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: The field strength of high-speed maglev millimeter wave (MMW) wireless communication systems is a direct reflection of system status and performance. In order to achieve state perception and fault detection under high-speed train operation conditions, it is necessary to accurately predict the field strength of the millimeter wave system. Firstly, an advanced field strength prediction model based on STAR module (FSPSTAR) is constructed for high-speed maglev MMW systems. The STAR module is utilized to extract feature dependencies between variables such as the current of the radio base station (RBS) demodulation module and the voltage of the frequency synthesizer module. Subsequently, linear projection is employed to obtain the temporal dependencies of the RBS demodulation module voltage variables. Finally, a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) module is used to integrate the relevant features and temporal characteristics of the variables to accomplish the prediction of the MMW system’s field strength. Validation using data collected from actual maglev train experiments shows that the root mean square error (RMSE) and the mean absolute error (MAE) of the FSPSTAR model’s prediction results are 51.9547 and 17.8825, respectively. The experimental results show that the model can achieve precise prediction of the field strengthof high-speed maglev train’s MMW systems.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Optimization Strategy for Smart Building Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In recent years, with the increasing importance of building energy consumption and energy-saving management, building energy consumption and carbon emissions in China account for approximately 20% of the national total. The application of intelligent control systems to optimize building operational efficiency has gained attention. These systems improve building load demand response while reducing operational costs. This study designs an adjustable load control model for building operations based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) technology, aiming to optimize both electricity cost and indoor temperature comfort. Using the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm as a stable baseline model, the agent can intelligently adjust air conditioning loads under fluctuating electricity prices and temperature constraints to minimize building operating costs. To test the model’s effectiveness, simulations were conducted on a test dataset containing actual load data. The results indicate that the model can effectively maintain indoor temperature within the target range over multiple periods while significantly reducing overall building load. This simulation validates the potential of deep reinforcement learning in complex building energy management and offers new insights for the development of building energy-saving control systems.

articleTitle: Classifying terrain for quadruped robots based on acoustic features
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Quadruped robots offer significant advantages in outdoor exploration missions due to their superior ability to adapt to variable terrains. Accurate terrain recognition enhances the robot’s motion control and safety. In recent years, acoustic signals have emerged as a powerful supplement for terrain recognition, owing to their robustness and fine-grained classification capabilities. This paper presents a terrain classification method for quadruped robots based on acoustic signatures, employing a ResNet-18 deep residual network to learn Mel spectrograms for efficient terrain classification and probability prediction. A directional microphone mounted on the robot captures sound signals generated during interaction with different terrains, and the Mel spectrograms are extracted as training data. The deep residual network is then trained on these spectrograms to achieve accurate terrain classification. To optimize real-time performance, this study also explores the impact of different audio segment lengths on classification accuracy, determining the optimal segment length to balance efficiency and response time. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and real-time performance in classifying three types of terrain-hard surface, grass, and sand—effectively meeting the terrain perception needs of quadruped robots in complex outdoor environments.

articleTitle: Image Retargeting Method Based on Grid Deformation and Content-Awareness
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This paper proposes an image retargeting method based on grid deformation and content awareness. The method adjusts the image to different sizes while preserving its prominent and structural features. It starts with a grid partitioning technique, where the image deformation is controlled by the coordinates of the grid vertices. This transforms the image retargeting problem into an optimization problem of the grid vertex coordinates. Simultaneously, saliency detection is performed, aiming to minimize the deformation of visually prominent objects while allowing more deformation of less noticeable elements, thus preserving the original structure. To protect linear features in the image, line segments need to be detected and these features incorporated into the energy equation to optimize the grid vertex coordinates. Experimental results demonstrate that the method provides visually pleasing retargeted images while retaining the original structural features.

articleTitle: A Rescheduling Method for Flexible Job Shops Based on an Improved Jaya Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel method that integrates an improved Jaya algorithm with simulated annealing to address the challenges of rescheduling in flexible job shops, particularly in scenarios involving urgent orders. The approach enhances global search and diversity by dividing the population into three subpopulations, each utilizing distinct mutation operators. Additionally, a reheating mechanism is introduced to effectively escape local optima. Experimental results on flexible job shop scheduling problems demonstrate the algorithm’s superior performance in both static scheduling and rescheduling tasks, achieving improved solution quality and efficiency compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: GatedUniPose: A Novel Approach for Pose Estimation Combining UniRepLKNet and Gated Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Pose estimation is a crucial task in computer vision, with wide applications in autonomous driving, human motion capture, and virtual reality. However, existing methods still face challenges in achieving high accuracy, particularly in complex scenes. This paper proposes a novel pose estimation method, GatedUniPose, which combines UniRepLKNet and Gated Convolution and introduces the GLACE module for embedding. Additionally, we enhance the feature map concatenation method in the head layer by using DySample upsampling. Compared to existing methods, GatedUniPose excels in handling complex scenes and occlusion challenges. Experimental results on the COCO, MPII, and CrowdPose datasets demonstrate that GatedUniPose achieves significant performance improvements with a relatively small number of parameters, yielding better or comparable results to models with similar or larger parameter sizes.

articleTitle: Vehicle Magnetorheological Semi-Active Suspension Variable Theory Domain Fuzzy Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In order to improve the safety and stability of the vehicle when entering the corner, the variable discourse domain fuzzy control strategy is introduced based on the adjustable damping characteristics of the semi-active suspension of magnetorheological(MR) damper. For this purpose, vehicle magnetorheological semi-active suspension dynamic model was constructed and the suspension forces at four wheels were obtained by combining the control algorithm and decoupling operation. The software was used to simulate and analyze the vehicle magnetorheological semi-active suspension on the C-class road surface, and the suspension performance was evaluated by the body vertical acceleration, suspension dynamic deflection and side inclination acceleration. The results show that compared with the passive suspension and the suspension with fuzzy controller, the suspension performance of MR Semi-active suspension system with variable discourse domain fuzzy control is significantly improved.

Author Keywords: variable discourse domain fuzzy control strateg

articleTitle: Pyramid Temporal-Spatial Attention Network for Traffic Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Traffic flow prediction is a crucial component in optimizing highway traffic within intelligent transportation systems. Achieving high-accuracy traffic flow predictions can lead to better management of intelligent transport systems, alleviating traffic congestion and reducing travel costs. However, traffic flows exhibit high spatiotemporal dynamics and nonlinear characteristics. Existing methods primarily focus on the spatiotem-poral features of traffic flows and often overlook the complexity of prediction. To fully explore the implicit spatiotemporal features of traffic flow data and reduce prediction loss, we propose a traffic flow prediction model that integrates a pyramid spatiotemporal attention mechanism. The model employs a dual-channel approach, embedding date and time encoding to capture temporal and periodic information, and combines it with traffic flow graphs to generate enhanced traffic flow data features. Based on this, a two-stage attention mechanism layer containing low-rank temporal attention and low-rank spatial attention is constructed, with a pyramid attention mechanism embedded externally beyond the two-stage attention mechanism layer that includes residual units. This forms a pyramid spatiotemporal attention module. Experiments conducted on public datasets indicate that the predictive performance of our model surpasses certain baseline models in terms of prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Discussion on the Foundation of Logic in Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In recent years, generative AI models such as ChatGPT, based on Transformer architectures, have developed rapidly and become a hot topic in society. They are widely used in programming, audio, and video processing fields, significantly enhancing productivity in these areas. However, various problems have also arisen during their application. At its core, generative AI still relies on symbolic formal logic and lacks the ability to simulate human cognitive patterns of understanding the world through prior logic or even dialectical logic. As such, it is impossible for these systems to achieve strong artificial intelligence as we know it. Currently, computer systems are founded on discrete mathematics and symbolic logic. This paper proposes an idea that combines prior logic theory with object-oriented programming techniques, using categorical judgment methods as a foundation to mimic human cognition patterns and discusses a possibility of approaching the realization of strong artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Action Intention Recognition based on L2 regularized LSTM-CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the advancement of industrial technology, intelligent manufacturing, and Industry 4.0, industrial exoskeleton technology has emerged as a pivotal component within the realm of intelligent manufacturing. Electromyographic signals (EMG) play an indispensable role in this domain. Given that the torso serves as a vital hub for human activities, accurate intention recognition holds immense significance in augmenting industrial production and facilitating the application of exoskeleton technology. In this study, we propose a hybrid algorithm framework that combines Long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for intent recognition of human body behavior. By collecting EMG data generated by healthy adult volunteers during specific tasks and normalizing them using fast Fourier transform, CNN is employed to extract spatial features of EMG signals while LSTM captures their temporal dynamics. Furthermore, L2 regularization is incorporated to effectively mitigate overfitting. Experimental results demonstrate an average accuracy rate of 97% in intent recognition tasks, showing excellent performance and potential practical applications in intelligent manufacturing and industrial exoskeleton.

articleTitle: An Overcurrent Protection Circuit for Low-Dropout Linear Regulators
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: To address the issue of excessive current in the power transistor during output short-circuit conditions in conventional overcurrent protection circuits for low dropout regulators (LDOs), this paper presents a novel overcurrent protection circuit for LDOs. By employing a common-source common-gate current mirror and voltage clamping principles, the sampling accuracy of the output current is enhanced. Additionally, a bypass branch is introduced to reduce the output current of the power transistor when the output voltage drops too low. Simulations using Cadence software demonstrate that the proposed overcurrent protection circuit effectively limits the current in the power transistor during output short-circuit conditions. Under an input voltage of 7 V, the LDO output voltage remains stable at 5 V, and when the output voltage drops to 0 V, the power transistor’s output current is reduced to $\mathbf{3 8 0. 4 0 2 \mu \mathrm { A }}$.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Operation Optimization Technique for Distributed Photovoltaic Integration into Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the increasing scale of distributed photovoltaic integration into distribution networks, the uncertain fluctuation characteristics of PV output power under power reverse feeding conditions result in frequent fluctuations in the operational status of distribution networks. To ensure the operational stability of distribution networks, an uncertainty operation optimization technique for distributed PV integration into distribution networks is proposed. The decision variables are selected as the points of common coupling and capacities of distributed PV power stations connected to the distribution network. Stochastic programming theory is utilized to calculate the uncertainty of PV active power, establishing a coordinated optimization model for distributed stochastic active and reactive power in distribution networks, thereby achieving uncertainty operation optimization of distribution networks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively enhance the stability of PV generation power, improve voltage control performance, shorten response time, and reduce annual operational line loss costs in distribution networks.

articleTitle: Spiking Neural Network based on YOLO-C3 for Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This research proposes a spiking neural network for object detection based on YOLOv5, in which the activation function in $\mathbf{C} 3$ module is replaced by a spiking neuron, and moved before the original initial module to better conform to the working principle of spiking neural network. Three different depths of spiking neural networks are studied, and their power consumption is theoretically analyzed. The proposed spiking neural network is tested by foreign objects detection on overhead power transmission line. Power consumption analysis and experimental results show that the proposed spiking neural network significantly reduces power consumption, while achieving detection accuracy higher than YOLOv8 and close to YOLOv5 Meanwhile, it can improve performance with increasing network depth.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization Deployment Method of Relay Network in Hydraulic Gate Opening and Closing Operation Scene
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In complex and severely obstructed outdoor conditions, the intelligent operation of hydraulic gantry cranes relies on the establishment of a highly reliable distributed sensor network. Given the demand for long-distance, lossless transmission of sensor data in such operational scenarios, this study proposes a mathematical model to quantify the interruption probability within relay networks. The objective is to reduce the frequency of network interruptions and optimize the configuration of relay nodes by establishing an appropriate optimization deployment framework. To effectively address this multi-objective optimization problem, this research improves upon the classical Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) and validates the feasibility and superiority of the proposed method through empirical case studies. The results indicate that the approach presented in this study can significantly reduce failure rates in relay networks while maintaining relatively low deployment costs, thereby providing effective support for the intelligent application of hydropower equipment.

articleTitle: Hand Gesture Controlled Robot Arm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In this paper we will be focusing on hand gesture controlled robot arms, the aim of this research is to develop an intuitive and easy to use system. For the purpose of demonstrating my proposed system and design, a prototype was made, the system is composed of two parts. The robotic arm is an articulated robot arm with 6 degrees of freedom that uses 6 servo motors (MG996R) to drive the joints, a servo driver (PCA9685), an Arduino Uno and a Bluetooth module (HC-05 / slave) for wireless connection.
