To address this problem, this paper proposes a Multidimensional ConvolutionDual Channel Transformer Network for efficient processing of point cloud data. The MCDTN framework consists of two branches: the main channel enhances the modeling of cross-channel features through dynamic attention to optimize feature representation; the auxiliary channel further improves fine-grained segmentation capabilities through encoders, multi-scale information interaction, and spatial attention. Experimental results show that MCDTN performs excellently in shape classification and part segmentation tasks, effectively reducing computational costs.

articleTitle: A Gait Recognition Algorithm Based on Global-Local Fusion and Adaptive Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Gait recognition is a biometric technology that identifies or verifies an individual’s identity by analyzing their walking patterns. In modern deep learning models, effectively integrating global and local features is crucial for enhancing the model’s perceptual and representational capabilities. To address this, we propose a gait recognition algorithm based on Global-Local Fusion and Adaptive Convolution. By integrating traditional 2D convolutions with adaptive convolutions, the algorithm leverages both global contextual information and local details. Additionally, incorporating a long-short temporal feature extraction module enables the model to simultaneously capture global dynamic information and local sequential details, significantly improving its ability to perceive complex temporal patterns. Extensive experiments on the CASIA-B dataset validate the superior performance of our model, achieving rank-1 accuracy rates of $\mathbf{9 7. 8 \%}, \mathbf{9 4. 3} \%$, and $\mathbf{8 3. 6 \%}$ under normal walking, carrying a bag, and wearing a coat conditions, respectively.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Based Visual Review Technology of Engineering Safety Design Documents
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: The accuracy and completeness of safety design documents are important indicators for ensuring the safe operation of engineering. Traditional document review methods suffer from issues such as relying on manual experience, time-consuming and error prone processes, and low efficiency. Based on this, this study proposes an efficient and accurate intelligent review method for engineering safety documents by combining artificial intelligence (AI) technology. This method integrates natural language processing, machine learning and other technologies, based on relevant specifications, legal provisions, relevant documents, experience and other review criteria, to review the content integrity and targeted solutions of design documents from two professional dimensions. Finally, the review results are evaluated and assisted in early warning, breaking through the limitations of traditional manual review, greatly improving review efficiency, and achieving refined intelligent review of engineering safety design documents.

articleTitle: MSCRep-YOLO: A new method for traffic sign recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This paper primarily addresses the challenges of small-scale traffic signs and real-time requirements in traffic sign recognition. We propose an improved YOLOv8n-based algorithm that incorporates a small object detection layer, a multi-scale convolutional attention mechanism, and a lightweight RepViT architecture, effectively enhancing detection capabilities for smallsized traffic signs while maintaining real-time performance. Additionally, the MPDIoU loss function replaces the Complete Intersection over Union loss function to further improve boundary regression performance. Tested on the TT100K dataset, the model achieves an 6.3% increase in precision, a 7% increase in recall, and an 7% increase in mean average precision, with only 78.82% of the original model’s parameters. These results demonstrate the model’s practical value in real-time traffic sign recognition tasks, especially in handling small-scale signs.

articleTitle: Design and Research of MEMS-Based Double-Layer Silicon Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Based on the interdigital structure, a microwave S band interdigital bandpass filter was proposed using silicon MEMS technology. While retaining the interdigital structure, the desired return loss was achieved by adjusting the distance between the vias and the resonator rods. Two filters were designed. The first filter has a center frequency of 21.4 GHz, a 1 dB bandwidth exceeding 2.5 GHz, an insertion loss of less than 1.5 dB, and a return loss greater than 15 db. Additionally, it achieves a stopband attenuation of more than 50 dB at frequencies of $\mathrm{f}_{\mathbf{0}} \pm 1.4 \mathrm{ghz} \mathrm{GHz}$. The filter’s compact dimensions are $(7 \times 2.8 \times 0.804) \mathrm{mm}^{3}$. The second filter has a center frequency of 5.5 GHz, a bandwidth of 1 GHz, an insertion loss of 2 dB, and a return loss exceeding 15 db. Its compact dimensions are also $(7.4 \times 5.9 \times 0.804) \mathrm{mm}^{3}$.

articleTitle: Research and Design of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Inspection System for Substation and Distribution Rooms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: The substation and distribution room is a critical component of the power distribution network, where the normal operation of its equipment is essential for the safety and reliability of the entire system. Therefore, promptly identifying and eliminating potential fault risks to ensure that the distribution equipment remains in optimal condition has always been a focal point for maintenance and operation personnel. This paper presents an intelligent inspection system for substation and distribution room equipment developed using artificial intelligence technology, along with corresponding software designed for real-time monitoring of equipment operational status. Furthermore, historical data can be conveniently queried through the backend software platform, effectively addressing the shortcomings associated with traditional manual inspections.

articleTitle: MCodec: A Codec Architecture integrated Mamba for Speech Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Recently, state space models have made significant progress in modeling sequential tasks, particularly the SSM-based Mamba network. Leveraging the efficient modeling of sequential data by the Mamba, we propose an end to end convolution-based codec architecture called MCodec that incorporates Mamba for speech enhancement tasks. The encoder of codec directly models the raw audio sampling points, performing downsampling and feature extraction akin to Mel-frequency spectra. Meanwhile, the decoder part, symmetrically mirroring the encoder, is utilized to reconstruct the waveform from the feature space, reducing reliance on manual feature extraction. Additionally, a bidirectional Mamba(Bi-Mamba) is introduced between these two components to extract deeper dependencies for speech reconstruction, effectively denoising the speech in the feature space. Experimental results demonstrates that the proposed model MCodec achieves promising improvements on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation and Analysis of Mulberry Orchard Intelligent Spraying Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: When the intelligent spraying robot is carrying out in the mulberry orchard fields, the robot chassis will be subjected to random vibrationcaused by the road surface, which will affect its bearing and walking capacity. If the robot is working in the vibration environment for a long time, fatigue damage may occur to its chassis and connecting parts, even lead to fracture or failure, the structural strength of the robot chassis will be seriously affected. In order to solve the above issues, the numerical simulation and analysis of the robot chassis are carried out on the basis of the random vibration theory in this paper. Firstly, a finite element model of the robot chassis with perfect grid quality is constructed and then numerical simulation is performed based on the Abaqus and the Power Spectral Density (PSD) curve in the national standard. The simulation results are shown that some parts of the robot chassis failed to meet the $\mathbf{3 \sigma}$ strength check standard, so that there are areas of excessive stress resulting in weak strength. Secondly, the numerical analysis is done on the grounds of the simulation results, the analysis results indicate that the partial structural optimization should be done for the weak position of the robot chassis and run the simulation again. Finally, the numerical simulation and analysis results show that the equivalent root-mean-square stress (RMISES) value of the robot chassis has decreased by 76% after structural optimization, from 383.3 MPa to 91.33 MPa. It can be seen that the optimized intelligent spraying robot is more suitable for mulberry orchard environment.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Genetic Search Approach for Electric Vehicle Routing with Time Windows
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This study addresses the Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (EVRPTW), where the fleet is composed of electric vehicles (EVs). In addition to load constraints, electric vehicles are also limited by battery capacity, which necessitate visits to charging stations during service. We further incorporates customer time window. We established a mathematical model for this problem and employ the Hybrid Genetic Search(HGS) algorithm for its resolution, marking the first application of this approach to the EVRPTW. Within the algorithm, we design a series of operators to construct customer service routes and insert charging stations. We conduct numerical experiments on various instances and compare the results with those of other researchers to showcase the efficacy of the proposed method and analyze the distinctive features of the problem.

articleTitle: Closed-loop Identification of Finite Impulse Response for Systems Subject to Complicated Disturbance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel method for identifying the Finite Impulse Response (FIR) of the closed-loop systems subject to complicated disturbance. The presented algorithm is a two-step robust identification method, which offers a solution to the challenge of dealing with complicated disturbance. The first step is to correct the process output in the frequency domain, and the second step is to identify the FIR parameters of model through the processed data. The illustrative simulation example serves to demonstrate the effectiveness of the presented approach.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Classification Research of Multi-class Motor Imagery EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of large parameter quantities and low operational efficiency faced by traditional deep learning models in EEG signal processing by proposing a model that integrates a One-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1DCNN) with a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). The model enhances signal class separability using One Versus Rest the Common Spatial Pattern (OVR-CSP) and strengthens key features through Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE), forming a dual-branch 1DCNN-TCN model for motor imagery EEG signal classification. Experimental validation on the BCI Competition IV 2a dataset demonstrates an average accuracy of $\mathbf{8 3. 1 3 \%}$. Compared to other advanced deep learning models, the training time is reduced by 8% to 23%, showcasing superior classification performance and efficient processing speed. This model offers a novel solution for EEG signal processing, making it particularly suitable for brain-computer interface systems that require rapid responses.

articleTitle: Control optimization of manipulator by introducing Bayesian polynomial interpolation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: When the six-axis manipulator moves in space, it is easy to cause the jump of joint Angle due to the mutation of speed and acceleration, and the motion trajectory has random fluctuations of faults, so it cannot move continuously. The interpolation function of the end effector of the manipulator is constructed based on the conventional cubic and quintic polynomial interpolation, and the motion trajectory planning method is optimized by using the Bayesian curve. Based on the standard D-H parameter method and forward kinematics, the mathematical model of the six-axis manipulator is established. And the Monte Carlo method is used to calculate the workspace of the manipulator. The three-five-cubic interpolation method and the Bayesian optimization method based on interpolation were used to obtain the values of Angle, angular velocity and angular acceleration respectively, and the motion trajectory planning was completed. Simulation results show that the proposed method can slightly improve the trajectory.

articleTitle: Design and application of error-compensated approximate multipliers
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In the context of the rapid development of electronic information technology, the rapid progress of emerging technologies such as the Internet of Things, big data analysis and artificial intelligence has posed unprecedented performance and power consumption challenges to computing systems. In many compute-intensive applications, completely accurate calculations are not always necessary. These applications tend to tolerate a certain level of calculation error. Therefore, it is a very effective idea to use approximate calculations and introduce errors in exchange for performance and power optimization. This thesis focuses on the study of approximate Booth multipliers and proposes a new approximate multiplier structure Approximate Error-compensated Booth Multipliers (AEBM), designed with error compensation. This includes an approximate Booth encoder, a newly proposed approximate 3-2 compressor and 4-2 compressor, and an approximate partial product array with error compensation based on the division of approximate factors. Compared to the structure discussed in [1], the key hardware performance indicator PDP of the AEBM structure is only 50.3%, and NMED is only 53.4%. Compared to [2], the PDP of the AEBM structure is 94%, and NMED is 1.4%, achieving a comprehensive design of accuracy and hardware performance. Finally, when applied to a neural network for image denoising, AEBM outperforms other approximate multipliers in terms of PSNR and SSIM. Compared with the exact multiplier, PSNR only loses 0.4, SSIM only loses $\mathbf{0. 0 1 5 8}$.

articleTitle: Optimization of Integrated Passenger and Cargo Cabins in Civil Aviation Through AI-Driven Design
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This study proposes an AI-based optimization approach for civil aviation passenger and cargo cabin design, focusing on maximizing space utilization, structural integrity, comfort, and energy efficiency.By combining deep learning for spatial feature extraction and reinforcement learning for dynamic layout optimization, the proposed method efficiently generates cabin configurations that meet multiple design objectives. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements over traditional design methods, with space utilization increasing by 16.2%, structural integrity enhanced by 17.3%, and energy consumption reduced by $\mathbf{2 2. 7 \%}$. This approach offers a novel, data-driven solution for optimizing cabin layouts, with potential applications in both commercial and freight aviation.

articleTitle: Vibration transmission characteristics of the palm of EVA gloves in a one-sixth-gravity, low-pressure environment
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: During extravehicular activities on the moon, the vibration generated by aerospace electric tools, transmitted through the EVA gloves to the hands, may lead to a decrease in the efficiency of astronauts’ work and even affect the smooth completion of aerospace missions. This study established a small-area palm local structural simulation model and a palm biomechanical dynamics model incorporating the structure of EVA gloves, and built a hand-transmitted vibration test platform simulating a low-pressure environment with one-sixth gravity. The results showed that the palm biomechanical dynamics model and simulation model can accurately predict the palm biomechanical dynamics response. Changes in EVA glove pressure have little effect on the palm vibration transmission rate. An increase in EVA glove pressure leads to an increase in the contact stiffness between the glove and the palm, resulting in a decrease in mechanical impedance, but does not affect the palm’s damping and effective mass.

articleTitle: Research on Image Depth Estimation Based on PatchMatchNet in the Field of Holographic 3D Display
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: The display effect of real objects in holographic 3D displays primarily depends on the accuracy of their depth and detail information. However, existing methods face challenges such as insufficient precision, high computational cost, and limitations on mobile devices. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multi-view depth estimation method based on PatchMatchNet(PMN). The method extracts image features using a feature extraction network and optimizes depth estimation through an adaptive propagation and evaluation mechanism, thereby enhancing the accuracy of object depth estimation. The obtained depth map is used to generate a hologram via tomography, which is then displayed as a holographic 3D image using a Spatial Light Modulator (SLM). Comparative analysis with openMVS and MVSNet demonstrates that PMN outperforms in terms of both depth estimation accuracy and computational efficiency, validating its practical application in holographic displays.

articleTitle: Research on the Smart Meter Data Collection System Based on Mobile Internet
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the rapid development of internet technology, traditional electric meters and meter-reading systems have become increasingly outdated, particularly in the context of growing electricity demands from large consumers, such as industrial enterprises, and the increasingly stringent requirements posed by the national grid in terms of supply and consumption mechanisms. To address these issues, we propose the development of a smart meter and smart meter reading system platform based on mobile internet technology.The system is divided into a three-tier network structure consisting of the user, substation, and host computer. Data exchange is conducted via the internet, with the host computer software running on a web server that users can access through their terminal computers and browsers. The host software is responsible for retrieving historical and real-time data from users and storing the historical data in a database. The user in this case refers to the smart meter, where each meter is equipped with a SIM card that has a unique IP address. The SIM card facilitates data exchange with the substation and host computer for data analysis. Based on users’ electricity consumption patterns and their peak and off-peak consumption curves, the system allocates electricity supply in an optimized manner and provides users with energy-saving recommendations to minimize electricity consumption.

articleTitle: Debertv3: Enhancing Text Quality Evaluation Ability
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This paper proposes an effective method to improve the accuracy of text quality evaluation. First, at the data layer, KerasNLP is used for dataset processing, converting pretrained text data into a format that can be accepted by the model. Next, the base pre-trained model is the DeBERTaV3 model, with a sigmoid activation function in the output layer. A Cosine Annealing learning rate scheduler is introduced to flexibly adjust the experimental learning rate and improve model efficiency. Finally, the weighted Kappa metric is used as the evaluation standard for the model’s prediction performance, ultimately achieving accurate assessment of text quality.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Non-Photorealistic Rendering (NPR) Generation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the advancement of deep learning technologies, non-photorealistic rendering (NPR) techniques have made significant breakthroughs in the field of computer graphics. This paper proposes a deep learning-based framework for NPR generation, combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs), aimed at automatically generating graphics in various artistic styles, such as sketches, ink paintings, and oil paintings. Through image style transfer and feature learning, the framework optimizes the preservation of details and enhances the artistic effects of the generated images. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional algorithms in terms of style transfer quality, generation efficiency, and adaptability. It shows strong potential for wide applications in animation, game design, and virtual reality, providing robust technical support for digital art creation.

articleTitle: Maintainability evaluation of machining center with small samples
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In recent years, some subsystems of machining center show the characteristics of long life, less faults and less maintenance. In these long-life subsystems, not only the maintenance data distributed in each subsystem is less, but also the prior information about the maintainability of the subsystem is less. In view of this situation, the lognormal distribution model is transformed into a normal distribution model, and a normal distribution small sample modeling method without prior information is used to establish the maintainability model of each subsystem. Then the maintainability of each subsystem is evaluated. The results show that the proposed method is obviously better than traditional large samples estimation method. The conclusion lays a foundation for the improvement measures of machining center credibility.

articleTitle: Semi-Supervised Learning based on Mass Conservation to improve Quality Predictions in a Polymer Pipe Production Process
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In polymer pipe production, achieving dimensional accuracy (diameter, wall thickness) is crucial but challenging due to the complexity of the process and its associated fluctuations. Consequently, accurate quality models are required to predict the pipe dimensions in advance to steer the process accordingly. Unfortunately, data scarcity is prevalent in industrial settings hindering the development of purely data-driven models while the integration of physical knowledge is largely neglected by existing work in this domain. Therefore, we propose a semi-supervised method based on mass conservation allowing the usage of synthetically generated data in addition to actual process measurements during the model training. The resulting method of physics-informed machine learning facilitates the training process and improves the generalizability of the resulting model in spite of small data sets. For validation purposes the data from an actual bi-oriented PVC pipe production process is used within a randomized cross-validation. It was shown that the proposed method produces superior results and reduces the mean squared error significantly by 41% to $\mathbf{6 0} \%$ when only 10 to $\mathbf{4 0}$ actual training samples are available. As a result, the prediction accuracy for pipe dimensions is notably increased allowing improved control of the process reducing dimensional fluctuations and material overweight despite data scarcity.

articleTitle: A hybrid strategy for parallel parking by combining geometric and optimization planners
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Path planning is a key function of automatic parking systems, especially for parallel parking in tight spaces. A qualified planner should compute quickly, ensure optimality, and avoid extra halfway stops. This paper proposes a hybrid strategy to make up the shortcomings of geometric path planners by optimizing the pose and heading angle at the first entry point into the parking space. Considering the number of maneuvers in the limited parking space, the computation of the entry point is described as a nonlinear programming problem, and solved by the genetic algorithm offline. Based on these, feasible paths for different parallel parking spaces can be directly provided online using the parametric form of circular arcs. The effectiveness of the hybrid strategy is validated by comparative tests in several parallel parking spaces of varying sizes, and the details about adjusting maneuvers in the parking space are discussed. Additionally, the traceability of the planned paths is verified by experimental tests.

articleTitle: A Novel 2-DOF Cable-Driven Flexible Manipulator Driven by Pneumatic Artificial Muscles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Cable-driven flexible manipulators are highly flexible and adapt well to complex, unstructured environments. Existing cable-driven flexible manipulators typically employ motor-driven actuators, which result in reduced inherent compliance and pose significant safety risks during interaction with the environment. To address these challenges, this study proposes a 2-DOF cable-driven flexible manipulator driven by pneumatic artificial muscles, with the aim of enhancing compliance and improving safety during interaction. Given the complexity and numerous internal components of the articulated joint segment, conventional dynamic analysis methods are difficult to apply effectively. To overcome these challenges and improve computational efficiency, an equivalent inverse dynamics model for the articulated joint segment is developed. To further improve trajectory tracking accuracy, a cable-length control algorithm based on “PID + feedforward compensation” is designed. Finally, a trajectory tracking simulation platform for the cable-driven flexible manipulator is constructed, validating the high-precision trajectory tracking performance of the control algorithm and further confirming the accuracy and effectiveness of the equivalent inverse dynamics model.

articleTitle: Research on an Improved Transformer-Based Model for Inland Vessel Fuel Consumption Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: To tackle the challenges of low accuracy and inefficiency in predicting inland vessel fuel consumption, an improved Transformer-based model is proposed. The model integrates Locally Linear Embedding (LLE), a patch embedding strategy, and a Two-Stage Attention (TSA) mechanism to enhance both prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. LLE reduces data dimensionality while preserving critical features, easing the training process. The patch embedding strategy streamlines time-series data processing, minimizing memory usage and accelerating training. The TSA mechanism, combining Content-Based Attention (CBA) and Self-Attention (SA), improves the model’s ability to capture intricate patterns. Experimental results show that the proposed model significantly outperforms traditional BP neural networks and LSTM models in fuel consumption prediction, achieving superior MSE and MAE metrics with shorter training times. This enhanced model offers a precise and efficient tool for fuel consumption prediction, supporting inland shipping companies in achieving sustainable development.

articleTitle: Real-Time Monitoring and Evaluation of Cutting Quality in Miniature Saw Machines Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In light of the growing demand for precision manufacturing, the real-time monitoring of cutting quality in micro sawing machines assumes great significance, with the objective of ensuring high cutting accuracy and efficiency. In this study, an innovative model based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) is proposed for the real-time monitoring and evaluation of cutting quality in micro sawing machines. Based on the existing ResNet architecture, the model introduces an attention mechanism to focus on the key features in the cutting mode and multi-scale feature fusion to enhance the detection ability of subtle defects. Furthermore, a temporal convolution module has been developed to capture the dynamic behaviour of the cutting process, thereby enabling the processing of video streams and the evaluation of quality trends in real time. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits an evaluation accuracy of over 95% on the cutting dataset of an industrial micro sawing machine. ()

articleTitle: Research on Vehicle Pedestrian Detection Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: To address the issues of vehicle pedestrian occlusion, missed detections, and false detections in traffic scene detection, an improved vehicle and pedestrian detection algorithm, YOLOv8_R, is proposed. Firstly, integrating the GAM attention module reduces feature information loss and enhances the focus on small object features. Secondly, the BiFPN is introduced to replace FPN and PAN, enabling adaptive fusion of multi-scale features. Thirdly, the loss function is optimized by replacing CIOU loss function with the Wise-IoU loss function, which increases the weight of difficult-to-distinguish samples. Finally, the dynamic detection head is used to improve the accuracy of detection while adapting to different detection tasks The results show that YOLOv8_R obtains 93.2% mAP on KITTI data set, which is 2.1 % higher than the original model, improving the accuracy of vehicle pedestrian detection, and alleviating the problems of occlusion and false detection to a certain extent.

articleTitle: Design of a multipurpose SCARA-like parallel robot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This design is based on a planar five-bar mechanism and combines the characteristics of parallel robots and SCARA robots to design a multipurpose SCARA-like parallel robot. Firstly, through requirement analysis, the actions that the multi-purpose SCARA-like parallel robot needs to perform are determined. Secondly, for the actions of this type of robot, mechanical structures are carried out based on the planar five-bar mechanism combined with parallel robots and SCARA robots, including the design of horizontal motion mechanism, vertical motion mechanism, and equipment support. Then, kinematic analysis, both forward and inverse, is conducted on the designed horizontal motion mechanism. Through analysis, it is concluded that with two motors, the horizontal motion mechanism can achieve movements forward, backward, left, and right, as well as predefined paths. Finally, a prototype is designed to verify the correctness of the analysis results and the rationality of the design.

articleTitle: Defect detection of reactor pressure vessel sealing surface based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Detecting the sealing surface of the reactor pressure vessel is essential for the safety and protection of nuclear energy. The traditional manual detection is inefficient and may cause irreparable harm to the human body. To solve these problems, this paper proposes an inspection method based on machine vision to replace manual inspection. This paper designs and compares deep learning algorithms that use different parameters and different processing functions for defect detection, and use Python language to complete data preprocessing, model training, and model prediction. Finally, the feature extraction and classification of the collected image are realized, and the defect detection of the sealing surface is completed.

articleTitle: A grasshopper-based path planning method for unsupported 3D printing of rotor models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Traditional three-dimensional (3D) printing technology generates objects and parts by depositing material layer by layer in the Z-axis direction. However, traditional printing processes require the creation of additional support structures when overhanging structures occur during the printing process. As a result, this technique requires additional material and increases the effective printing time. To overcome these problems, this paper this paper proposes a grasshopper based path planning method for supportless material printing. A series of surfaces are computed by extracting the outer contour lines of the model and the original model is sliced on the surfaces and the five-axis printing G-code generated from the slices will print the original model. The feasibility of the method is demonstrated and unsupported continuous path planning with surface layering is realized.

articleTitle: Manufacturing Process Selection Using Graph Neural Networks: A Novel Approach to CAD Model Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Manufacturing process selection, as a core element in the manufacturing workflow, plays a crucial role in improving processing efficiency and manufacturing quality. However, due to the fragmented, experience-based, and often outdated nature of processing knowledge, current process selection methods heavily rely on human intervention. To address these challenges, this study proposes an innovative approach that reframes manufacturing process selection as a graph-based semantic segmentation task. Building on this concept, we introduce a graph neural network-based method for manufacturing process selection, capable of effectively identifying processing methods in CAD models. This method discretely samples the topological faces and edges of CAD models, storing them as node and edge attributes in an attributed adjacency graph. Finally, we design experiments to validate the effectiveness and accuracy of this method in identifying manufacturing processes. Experimental results demonstrate that representing 3D CAD models with attributed adjacency graphs effectively captures the geometric and topological relationships between different faces of the model. This method can accurately identify corresponding manufacturing processes at the topological face level of CAD models, offering a novel approach to automated process selection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Human-Exoskeleton Interaction through Kinematic and Dynamic Analysis of Hip Exoskeleton Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Exoskeleton robots, as tangible designs within the computer-human interaction (CHI) field, hold significant potential for enhancing human performance in activities such as walking, running, and ascending or descending stairs. However, misalignments between the human body and the exoskeleton can lead to discomfort due to undesired torques and relative motion. This study seeks to improve human-exoskeleton interaction (HEI) by optimizing the mechanism design to ensure better alignment. The study begins with an analysis of the degrees of freedom in the hip exoskeleton robot (HER), followed by kinematic and dynamic simulations of HEI. Experimental results indicate that the designed HER achieves misalignment compensation (MC) displacements ranging from 0 to 18.075 mm. When compared to HER assistance without MC, the proposed design increases assistance efficiency by $\mathbf{4 2 \%}$, significantly enhancing wearing comfort. This work lays the groundwork for the integration of advanced sensing and intelligent control systems into exoskeleton mechanisms, paving the way for broader applications in rehabilitation and motion enhancement.

articleTitle: Low-repair array codes based on nested structures
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: To address the problem of low repair efficiency of single- and double-disk of localized horizontal array code, this paper retains the original advantages of horizontal array code, transforms it on the basis of RDP 2D array code, and proposes a 2D array code model based on nested structure - NRDP (Nested Rows Diagonal Parity Code). The overall layout of the NRDP code is the same as that of the RDP code. However, when deploying data columns, the NRDP code deploys the RDP code of one prime number level smaller as a whole in the data columns of the NRDP code, forming a nested relationship. The increased redundant data reduce the repair overhead and error recovery time. Through theoretical analysis, NRDP has good compiled code complexity, improves the problem of uneven reading and writing during disk repair, and reduces the total amount of data that needs to be read during single- and double-disk failures, improving the success rate of single- and double-disk repair. The experimental results show that compared with RDP, LRRDP, and DRDP, NRDP can save $7.03 \%-\mathbf{3 0. 0 1 \%}$ of the single-disk failure repair time and $14.79 \%-26.51 \%$ of the dual-disk repair time.

articleTitle: Underwater Object Detection Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This paper proposes the underwater target detection algorithm CMUOD based on YOLOv8 to address the issues of varying scales, low clarity, and overlapping of underwater targets. The main contribution of this article includes introducing an attention mechanism to extract key attention regions from a large amount of global information, thereby further reducing the model’s missed and false detection rates. In addition, we propose the Multi-scale Hybrid Space Pyramid Pool Fast (MHSPPF) module, which can avoid losing more information in max pooling and improve the detection performance of the model. Finally, we conducted comparative experiments on the UPR dataset and demonstrated the results. The experimental results show that the mAP score of our proposed CMUOD algorithm is 89.7 %, which is 5.3% higher than DETR. This indicates that the proposed detection method is particularly suitable for underwater object detection tasks.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Data Fusion and Anomaly Detection in Industrial IoT Systems Using Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for heterogeneous data fusion and anomaly detection in Internet of Things (IoT) systems using spatio-temporal graph neural networks (GNNs). The framework addresses the challenges of integrating multi-source data and capturing complex spatiotemporal dependencies in industrial environments. A multi-layer GNN architecture with a spatio-temporal attention mechanism is developed to learn hierarchical representations of industrial entities and their interactions. Extensive experiments on real-world IoT datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed approach over state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. The framework shows robustness to parameter changes and scalability to large-scale datasets, making it suitable for real-time anomaly detection in industrial settings. This work contributes to the advancement of intelligent and reliable industrial operations in the context of Industry 4.0.

articleTitle: Secure and Efficient Cross-Domain Access Control for Industrial Internet Alliance Chains Based on Zero-Knowledge Proof
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cross-domain access control mechanism for industrial Internet alliance chains using zero-knowledge proof (ZKP). The mechanism integrates ZKP with blockchain technology to achieve secure, privacy-preserving, and decentralized access control across multiple industrial domains. A formal system model and security framework are presented, along with an efficient ZKP protocol for attribute-based access control. The proposed scheme is implemented using smart contracts and distributed ledger technology. Comprehensive performance analysis and security verification demonstrate the mechanism’s high throughput, low latency, and resilience against various security threats. Experimental results show that the proposed solution is scalable and practical for large-scale industrial Internet scenarios, enabling secure data sharing and collaboration while protecting user privacy and ensuring fine-grained access control.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic flowmeter fault early warning method based on Bayesian optimization XGBoost
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: To accurately identify the abnormal operating status of ultrasonic flowmeters in advance, a fault warning method for the key parameters of ultrasonic flow meters based on Bayesian optimization and XGBoost algorithm is proposed. The method involves effective data preprocessing techniques applied to historical operational data from the remote online diagnostic system of the measurement system. A prediction model for the key parameters of ultrasonic flow meters is built using the Bayesian optimization approach combined with XGBoost algorithm. The fault warning limits for the key parameters of ultrasonic flow meters are determined based on the three-sigma criterion. The results of the experimental tests demonstrate that the proposed method can detect the abnormal operating status of the key parameters of ultrasonic flow meters in advance. Comparative analysis with lightGBM and CatBoost algorithms reveals that the XGBoost model optimized by Bayesian optimization exhibits significant advantages in terms of computational time and model regression evaluation.

articleTitle: Predicting Machine RUL by Injecting Reflection-Padded Convolutional Outputs from Time Series Reconstruction into a Multi-Layer Perceptron
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of machinery is a critical component of Prognostics and Health Management (PHM), as it enables proactive maintenance, reduces downtime, and optimizes asset utilization. In this paper, we present a new approach for predicting the RUL, where time series reconstruction is employed and reflection-padded results of convolutional layers are further injected into a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP). Time-series reconstruction reorganizes one-dimensional temporal data into two-dimensional formats. It broadens the spatial and temporal receptive fields of convolutional layers so that spatial and temporal dependencies can be effectively captured. By applying reflection padding to preserve boundary features and increasing data diversity, this method is able to extract more robust features. The convolutional outputs of the modules with reflection-padding are then input into an MLP so that the nonlinear mappings of the MLP can give significant improvements regarding RUL estimation. Empirical evaluations conducted on the C-MAPSS dataset show that the proposed architecture is beneficial in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness, which outperforms traditional MLP and CNN models by significant margins and achieves the best performance among the previously proposed state-of-the-art models.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Shielding Structure Design and Shielding Performance of Key Components in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Electric vehicles emit electromagnetic radiation energy during normal operation, and harmful electromagnetic radiation can severely affect the normal operation of sensitive components inside the vehicle. The study centers on metal grid electromagnetic shielding structures, analyzing the influence of parameters like grid cell period and linewidth on optical and electromagnetic shielding performance, while comparing the shielding efficiency of different metal grid shapes. Additionally, a novel and effective metal grid electromagnetic shielding structure was designed for a specific model of electric vehicle. This structure achieves a shielding efficiency of over ${9 0 \%}$ in the ${2 - 2 0} \mathrm{G H z}$ frequency band, with a maximum shielding effectiveness of 33.5 dB, aimed at protecting the sensitive components inside the vehicle. Metal grid component samples were manufactured using a liquid metal injection molding method within trenches formed by photopolymerized 3D printing. The developed metal grid shielding structure exhibits an effective electromagnetic shielding range from $3-20 \mathrm{GHz}$, achieving a peak shielding efficiency of 24.8 dB, indicating satisfactory shielding performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Video Quality Assessment through Semantic Guidance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of network and information technologies, user-generated content (UGC) platforms like TikTok have become essential mainstream media channels. However, video quality often varies significantly due to factors during shooting, compression, and transmission, inconveniencing users. While existing methods assess video quality using objective standards, human subjective perception remains crucial. This paper introduces a simple and effective no-reference video quality assessment model that integrates human perception into the complex video generation process to enhance UGC quality evaluation. We develop a trainable FastVQA branch to extract technical features and incorporate a ConvNeXt branch to capture semantic features. These features are combined and processed through a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) network to predict video quality scores. Our findings demonstrate that incorporating semantic features allows the network to better leverage human perception of video content quality, thereby improving the accuracy of technical assessments. This method not only optimizes traditional quality assessment models but also offers a new research direction, highlighting the importance of human perception in automated video quality evaluation.

articleTitle: Aspect-Level Sentiment Analysis Based on Part-of-Speech Enhanced and Graph Convolution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Although graph neural networks based on syntactic information have achieved good results in aspect-level sentiment analysis, these methods still have certain limitations and often struggle with accurately processing the semantic and syntactic information between aspect words and opinion words. Therefore, we propose an aspect-level sentiment analysis Based on part-of-speech enhanced and graph convolution network(PSEGCN). Specifically, we design a part-of-speech attention mechanism combined with self-attention to obtain an enhanced semantic adjacency matrix. By focusing on important part-of-speech words, this approach strengthens the semantic correlation between aspect words and opinion words while reducing noise from irrelevant words. Next, we construct an aspect-distance-based adjacency matrix from the original dependency tree and combine it with the dependency relationship adjacency matrix. This fused matrix allows for a more comprehensive learning of the syntactic information of aspect words. Additionally, we use two GCN networks to encode the information from the two matrices. Finally, we use a gated mechanism function to better integrate syntactic and semantic information for sentiment classification. Our model achieved accuracy rates of 0.7816 on the laptop dataset and 0.7565 on the Twitter dataset, outperforming all baseline models, which demonstrates the effectiveness of our model.

articleTitle: Accurate preference modeling for sequential recommendation with adaptive denoising and attention
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: The fundamental objective of sequential recommendation is to meticulously analyze the user’s historical interaction behavior and accurately capture their preferences in order to predict the subsequent items that the user may be interested in. However, existing approaches predominantly focus on the interaction characteristics between users and items as well as the attributes of the items themselves, and tend to overlook the time-series dynamics of user preferences, including their longterm and short-term fluctuations. In addition, factors such as user misuse and system exposure bias may lead to noise in real-world interaction data, which poses significant challenges to the accuracy of the model. To address these challenges, we have designed an innovative model architecture that not only recognizes and corrects noise in the input initial item sequences, but also fuses users’ long-term and short-term preferences based on the corrected interaction sequences using a hierarchical attention mechanism to more realistically map users’ true preferences. In order to train our model to recognize and remove noise, we design two self-supervised learning mechanisms: deletion recovery and insertion removal. We conduct a comprehensive series of experiments on three real datasets and show that our model outperforms state-of-the-art sequential recommendation baseline models.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Appearance Model Update Method for Target Tracking Based on Prior Confidence
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: For the challenges posed by rapid changes in target scale and appearance due to the high-speed motion of aerial vehicles during the infrared imaging terminal guidance phase, an adaptive appearance model update method for target tracking based on prior confidence is proposed. This method uses OSTrack [1] as a baseline and comprehensively analyzes historical confidence variation information within a specified time window to assess the adaptability of the current appearance model and determine the timing for appearance updates. By analyzing the confidence performance of historical prediction results, reliable samples are selected to construct template information adaptively updating the target appearance model. This enhances the robustness and stability of the algorithm throughout the terminal guidance phase. Simulation results for infrared terminal guidance indicate that, compared to the baseline algorithm, the proposed method improves the success rate by 5% and increases accuracy by 4.8%. This approach provides an effective solution for enhancing the performance of infrared guidance systems.

articleTitle: MVP-MCTS: Language Modelling a Flexible Multi-Agent Planning Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Large language models have come under the spotlight in recent years for their seemingly multifaceted capabilities which extend far beyond text processing. In particular, they have been shown to possess logical and reasoning capabilities, which has been augmented in various ways via the use of inference frameworks such as reasoning trees and planning graphs. Meanwhile, some studies tried to explore tasks that are not limited to single-agent scenarios, focusing on tasks in multi-agent settings. However, most of their works focus on text-based role-playing games, while long-term planning games have yet to be extensively explored. In this work we extend the reasoning and planning abilities of the language model to coordinate between multiple agents which have been tasked to achieve specific goals with the least amount of resource expenditure. We devise the framework MVP-MCTS: Multi-agent Value-coordination and Prompt-based Monte-Carlo Tree Search(MCTS) that integrates the prompting of a language model with a tree search procedure without the need for additional grounding. Our method relies on task-specific prompting and the innate world model of the LLM to perform search space simulation and decision-making. Our experiments show that our framework is able to outperform current state-of-the-art LLMdriven planning frameworks.

articleTitle: Framework and Function Design of Machine Learning Platform for Power Generation Process
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the transformation of China’s energy structure, the control requirements for the power generation process are becoming increasingly precise and intelligent. Applying machine learning algorithms to improve operational efficiency has become one of the important demands of current power generation enterprises. However, the deployment of various machine learning technologies that have already been put into operation in the power generation process is independent of each other, and the data interaction ability with the control system is limited. This not only makes the station lack of a unified operations and maintenance management entrance, but also requires a large amount of manual operation to complete the entire process from model training to inference, making it difficult to update the model. This paper proposes a framework and function design of the machine learning platform for the power generation process aming at the data characteristics and control system operation mode of the power generation production site. It provides a programming and management interface based on algorithm modules in a graphical interface. At the same time, the platform’s ability to obtain historical and real-time data of the production site is achieved by coupling the training program and inference program with the control system, so that all machine learning processes can be included in the platform’s automated operation scope. The application of this platform can facilitate users to complete customized model training for selected production processes, efficiently complete machine learning tasks without affecting the normal operation of the control system, reduce the manpower and learning costs of applying machine learning technology, and provide a feasible solution for power generation enterprises to improve their intelligent operation level.

articleTitle: Tabular Data Classification Method Based on Image Transformation and Capsule Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Due to the fundamental differences in structure between tabular data and image data, CNNs (Convolutional Neural Networks) are challenging to apply directly to the analysis and classification of tabular data. To address this issue, we propose an innovative method for classifying tabular data, combining tabular-to-image transformation techniques with Capsule Networks. First, we employ a consensus clustering method based on multiple subspace weighting to group features, ensuring the stability and consistency of the groupings. Next, we introduce a method to convert each data instance into a two-dimensional pixel image, using the ant colony algorithm to optimize pixel layout. Finally, the generated images are fed into an improved Capsule Network for classification prediction. Experimental results from 11 multidimensional tabular datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves classification accuracy compared to existing tabular data transformation methods. Furthermore, due to the smaller size of the generated images, the complexity of the model is reduced, which improves computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Deadlock-Free Scheduling of Flexible Manufacturing Systems Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Flexible manufacturing system can meet the demand of personalized and small-lot production due to its flexibility and resource sharing characteristics, but the deadlock problem that may occur during its scheduling process will seriously affect the production efficiency, so effective deadlock-free scheduling is called the key challenge of flexible manufacturing system re. Traditional deadlock-free scheduling methods have problems such as high scheduling complexity and inability to fully utilize resources, etc. In this paper, Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) is applied to the deadlock-free problem of flexible manufacturing system, and a DF-DQN model is proposed, which combines the structural features of Petri net, enhances the model’s ability to express the state of the system, and introduces a deadlock recovery mechanism, which further improves the scheduling reliability and efficiency, and guarantees the deadlock-free scheduling. While ensuring deadlock-free scheduling, it improves resource utilization and productivity. Comparative experimental results show that the model outperforms the traditional method in reducing the deadlock rate and the maximum completion time, which verifies its effectiveness in deadlock prevention and scheduling optimization.

articleTitle: An improved model based on YOLOv8 for tiny object detection in the maritime environment
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: To address the issue of low accuracy in maritime tiny target detection, this paper presents an optimized maritime tiny target detection model based on YOLOv8. Firstly, the Spatial tiny target detection model based on YOLOv8. Firstly, the Spatial and Channel Reconstruction Convolution (SCConv) and the Cascaded Group Attention Mechanism (CGA) are introduced to optimize the original C2f module in the backbone of YOLOv8. SCConv helps reduce spatial and channel redundancy, thereby enhancing the model’s efficiency without incurring additional computational costs. Meanwhile, CGA is conducive to enhancing the focus on significant targets, resulting in an efficient improvement of the model’s detection performance. Secondly, the the focus on significant targets, resulting in an efficient improvement of the model’s detection performance. Secondly, the P2-tiny target detection layer and the GhostConv module are adopted to enhance the model’s ability to detect tiny targets and reduce the number of parameters in the model. Finally, G-ELAN reduce the number of parameters in the model. Finaliy, G-ELAN is introduced to replace the C2f module in the neck to deepen the network depth and enhance the model’s feature extraction capability. The improved model is trained and validated on the SeaDronesSee Object Detection V2 dataset. The results indicate SeaDronesSee Object Detection $V 2$ dataset. The resuits indicate that our model improves the precision and mAP mA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> by 3.9% and $\mathbf{8. 5 \%}$, respectively, compared to the YOLOv8 base model. 8.5%, respectively, compared to the YOLOv8 base model. Compared with other newly released YOLO models, our approach also exhibits good performance in the maritime tiny target detection task.

articleTitle: Transformer-Based Differential Superpixel Selection Network for Remote Sensing Images Change Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In remote sensing images change detection, the results of Transformer often face the low precision and edge fitting problems, which are caused by the highly complex background of building categories and the imbalance of sample ratio. To address these challenges, we propose a Transformer-based differential superpixel selection network. First, a differential superpixel selection module is proposed which introduces difference selecting to refine the edge feature representation of the object region by using the boundary information of the selected superpixel. Second, we propose a multi-scale feature-aware enhancement module, which fuses multi-scale feature differences with the features extracted by the hierarchical Transformer encoder. This module enhances difference awareness while suppressing interference from complex backgrounds. Finally, we construct a composite loss function that combines the focal loss function with the binary cross-entropy loss function. The composite loss function can pay more attention to hardly classifying samples and suppress the influence of easily classifying samples. Our proposed algorithm is tested on the widely used LEVIR-CD and DSIFN-CD datasets. The results show that it effectively improved detection accuracy and edge fitting compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: A Survey of Mixture Models for Scientific Literature
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: The emergent abilities of large language models (LLMs) in knowledge understanding and problem reasoning has garnered considerable interest from both academic and industrial sectors. The data processing of LLMs has expanded from textual data to multimodal data, including images, formulas, videos, and charts, leading to a sharp increase in model parameters and computational power requirements. Mixture models are one of the solutions to these issues, but research on mixture models for the understanding of scientific literature data remains scarce. This paper outlines the application of LLMs in the field of knowledge engineering and analyzes the importance of multi-model data LLMs in the intelligence domain. Then, this paper first conducts a review analysis of research on mixture models in scientific literature understanding, analyzing respective research directions and related work from three aspects: multimodal data understanding, dynamic expert scheduling strategies, and expert domain-specific training. Finally, this paper summarizes the current state of research on mixture models for scientific literature and looks forward to specific research directions in this field. Scientific literature, as an important carrier of human knowledge, is the core key supporting innovation. Existing research mainly focuses on the general application of mixture models. For the first time, this paper conducts a review analysis of mixture model research specifically for the field of scientific literature.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Safe and Efficient Human-Machine Collaborative Autonomous Driving Systems: Addressing Challenges in Interaction, System Downgrade, and Driver Intervention
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In the realm of intelligent vehicles, the collaborative driving mode between autonomous systems and human drivers is regarded as a long-term developmental trend. This paradigm integrates autonomous systems, drivers, and road environments, necessitating the design of a safe and efficient human-machine co-driving system due to its inherent complexity. This study delves into the interaction mechanisms of human-machine co-driving, clarifies the types of driver takeover scenarios, and thoroughly examines the multifaceted challenges encountered during system downgrade, including the accuracy of motion prediction, driving risk assessment, driver state monitoring, vehicle state information analysis, and the optimization of human-machine interaction interfaces. To address these challenges, we propose a series of design recommendations: enhancing the efficacy of autonomous driving systems through dimensionality reduction strategies; bolstering system robustness with redundant environmental perception; constructing advanced prediction and risk assessment models; establishing a comprehensive driver state evaluation system; optimizing vehicle state information analysis during takeover processes; and designing intuitive human-machine interaction interfaces. The aim is to develop a co-driving system that not only leverages the strengths of autonomous driving but also ensures the effective intervention of drivers when necessary, thereby providing robust theoretical support and practical guidance for the construction of safe, efficient, and intelligent autonomous driving human-machine collaborative systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of Multi-Resource Scheduling Strategies in Distributed Training Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In large-scale model training, distributed training frameworks offer an effective solution to the limitations of a single GPU or node in handling massive model parameters and datasets. By distributing training tasks across multiple nodes, distributed model training enables parallel utilization of computational resources, significantly improving training efficiency. However, efficient scheduling of multi-resources (such as computation, storage, and network) in distributed environments remains a critical challenge. This paper proposes an optimized multi-resource scheduling strategy that integrates Kubernetes’ scheduling principles. By improving the scheduling algorithm, the strategy effectively enhances resource utilization and task completion efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces task waiting time and improves overall system throughput in distributed environments.

articleTitle: Application study of AIGC technology in the precision detection of engine parts
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: This paper summarizes the application research of AIGC (artificial intelligence generated content) in the precision detection of engine parts in recent years, and discusses its key role in the detection efficiency, precision improvement and manufacturing automation. Through the analysis of relevant literature, this paper summarizes the application cases of AIGC technology in specific components such as spark plug, valve ring, etc., and analyzes the challenges and the future development direction of the technology in practical application.

articleTitle: Research on Attitude Control of Underwater Unmanned Autonomous Vehicle Recovery Platform Based on Active Disturbance Rejection Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In response to the issues of susceptibility to disturbances and slow response speed in attitude adjustment during the recovery process of underwater unmanned submersibles, this paper proposes an attitude control method based on anti-disturbance sliding mode control. Firstly, the kinematic and dynamic mathematical models of the underwater recovery platform are established. Secondly, by integrating sliding mode control with anti-disturbance control, a new type of anti-disturbance sliding mode controller is developed. This controller can monitor and compensate for both internal and external disturbances (For example, ocean currents) of the system and relies on sliding mode control to ensure rapid and stable attitude adjustments. Finally, simulations are performed in the Matlab/Simulink environment and compared with traditional sliding mode control and PID control. The results demonstrate that the underwater unmanned submersible recovery platform control system based on anti-disturbance sliding mode control proposed in this paper exhibits high precision and meets the requirements for rapid attitude adjustment. The control method presented in this paper can provide valuable reference for attitude control of underwater recovery platforms.

articleTitle: A fusion model combining improved A* algorithm and dynamic window approach for path planning of obstacle-overcoming robots
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: as traditional path planning methods often face difficulties and reach excessively long paths when planning paths for mobile robots in complex environments, a novel method that combines the improved $\mathrm{A}^{*}$ algorithm and the dynamic window approach (DWA) is proposed here for path planning of obstacle-overcoming robots. Specifically, point cloud data are obtained by 3D laser radar (LiDAR) scanning and the discrete noises are removed by radius filtering, and the elevation information of each grid is computed to construct raster maps with elevation data; the obstacle region is divided into an obstacle-avoidance area and an obstacle-overcoming area as per the robot’s obstacle-overcoming capacity. Next, based on the improved $\mathrm{A}^{*}$ algorithm and the obstacle-overcoming function, the path return mechanism is introduced to reduce the length of the planned path and number of corner-turnings, thereby optimizing the planned path. Last, the key points in global path planning are set as the target points of the DWA to fuse global and local planning. Experiments reveal that our fusion model has significantly cut the length of the planned path and improved the path-planning flexibility and efficiency of the obstacle-overcoming robot.

articleTitle: Knowledge Graph Embedding using Tri-Relation Vectors on Hyperplanes
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Graph neural networks are a subfield of graph learning within artificial intelligence. Knowledge graphs enhance information interconnectivity and comprehensibility by representing knowledge in a structured and semantic manner. They provide richer semantic information compared to traditional datasets by explicitly modeling relations and entities. Knowledge graphs play a key role in powering search engines, answering questions, and providing recommendations. A major focus of research in this area is link prediction, which aims to uncover missing relationships between entities that have not yet been recorded. Knowledge graph embedding, a highly efficient and scalable approach for link prediction. This paper focuses on distance-based models for KGE, which are lightweight, easy to train, and geometrically interpretable. We propose a new model, TriRH, which uses tri-relation vectors on hyperplanes to enhance predictive accuracy and overall model performance. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that TriRH achieves better performance than existing models across multiple metrics.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheduling of Cascade Pumping Stations Based on Improved Northern Goshawk Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: To address the issues of low efficiency and high energy consumption in cascade pump stations systems, this study developed an optimization scheduling model and solved it using the Northern Goshawk Optimization (NGO). NGO features a fast convergence rate and high optimization accuracy. However, NGO is prone to falling into local optima during the solving process. To overcome this issue, the Subtraction-Average-Based Optimizer and Cauchy mutation are combined to propose an Improved Northern Goshawk Optimization (INGO). Experimental tests using benchmark functions showed that the INGO demonstrated significant advantages in optimization performance. INGO was applied to the optimization scheduling of the three-level pump stations in Shanxi Province’s Wanjiazhai Yellow River Diversion Project, verifying its feasibility and effectiveness for solving cascade pump stations scheduling problems. The results showed that, compared to existing schemes, the INGO-based optimization scheme improved the efficiency of cascade pump stations operation by $1.09 \%-1.43 \%$, surpassing the efficiency achieved by NGO.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Big Data Technology in the Field of Coal Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the in-depth application of various intelligent sensors in the coal mine, although the coal mining industry is gradually transforming from automation to intelligence, a large amount of operational monitoring data is generated in the production process, and the total amount of data is still on a growing trend every year, and the traditional decentralized data management system can no longer satisfy the data storage and processing requirements under the condition of big data due to the limitation of computing resources. To address the above issues, big data technology is applied to coal mine data management system, develop coal mine intelligent big data management system, and utilize big data frameworks such as Hadoop and Spark to build a distributed parallel processing environment, which constitutes a computing cluster with a unified resource scheduling of dispersed computing resources, and makes full use of idle storage resources and computing resources. Firstly, the data collected by various subsystems in the underground coal mine are standardized, and the data of various subsystems are unified and integrated, and then the collected data are analyzed and utilized using big data processing technology, and the invalid data and abnormal data are compressed, cleaned and stored hierarchically according to the access timeliness, so as to expand the horizontal and vertical storage capacity of the current decentralized data management system in the coal mine. The actual application effect shows that applying big data technology to the coal mine management system can integrate the scattered data resources of the coal mine and improve the reading and writing ability and processing ability of the data.

articleTitle: Customer Churn Prediction Based on Multiscale Attention and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Most of the feature extraction methods for telecommunication customer churn research tend to lose important information from other scales by stacking the single-scale receptive field information, which leads to limited prediction effect. To address this problem, this paper proposes a customer churn risk prediction model based on a multi-scale convolutional attention module-convolutional neural network. Firstly, the features are reshaped into a form similar to grey scale images, thus allowing the 2D convolutional neural network to extract local spatial features, and using residual blocks to enhance the information flow of the deep network. Based on this, a multi-scale convolutional attention module is designed in this paper to effectively capture multi-scale feature information and enhance feature diversity from different domains, while adaptively learning the weights of each feature channel and feature map pixel point. Ten-fold cross-validation experiments are conducted on two publicly available benchmark datasets, and in order to enhance the recognition ability of the proposed model for minority class instances, SMOTENN is introduced to over-and under-sample the telecom datasets used, and the results show that the proposed model outperforms the comparison model in terms of the scores on Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score, providing a better decision-making reference for telecom service providers to identify churn.

articleTitle: Method for Qin Bamboo Slip Text Detection Based on an Enhanced DBNet Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: An improved DBNet-based detection method is proposed to address the detection challenges posed by background interference, texture breakage, and dense arrangements in the text of unearthed Qin bamboo slips. This approach incorporates a text collaborative learning module and an adaptive weighted feature pyramid into the DBNet framework. ResNet18, augmented with deformable convolution and the text collaborative learning module, is utilized during the feature extraction stage. Features of characters and blank areas are collaboratively sampled through a convolutional cascade with varying receptive fields, effectively mitigating the issue of texture breakage. The enhanced adaptive weighted feature pyramid optimizes the feature map’s receptive field and attention fusion, improving the model’s ability to learn complex backgrounds and densely arranged text.
