Furthermore, the modified loss function applies bilateral upsampling to improve the adaptability of the binarization process. Experimental results on the synthetic Qin bamboo slips text detection dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 99.82%, with F -score and recall rates of 97.02% and 94.38%, respectively-marking improvements of 1.35% and 2.05% over the original DBNet model. These results highlight the method’s superior performance and balanced effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research on the Remaining Useful Life Prediction Model of Complex Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence technology, the development of intelligent manufacturing has become an inevitable trend. Utilizing AI technology to ensure the safe operation of factories is a crucial aspect of smart factories. In particular, research focused on fault diagnosis and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction models based on machine learning has garnered significant attention from both academia and industry. This paper explores RUL prediction models for complex equipment, introduces four representative models, and analyzes their performance using two benchmark datasets, C-MAPSS and N-CMAPSS. Finally, the paper discusses the future research and application trends of artificial intelligence technology in complex equipment operation and maintenance.

articleTitle: Towards Enhanced Privacy and Usability in Trajectory Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Trajectory data contains critical information about individual behavior habits and moving patterns, making it invaluable for applications such as traffic planning, urban management, business decision-making, etc. However, sharing this data raises significant privacy concerns, as it can expose sensitive details about individuals. This has created a pressing need for synthetic, privacy-preserving trajectory data in location-based applications. While differential privacy techniques generate synthetic trajectories by adding noise to probabilistic models and resampling, they often produce coarsegrained results that fail to reflect realistic movement paths, leading to poor usability. Recently, deep learning approaches learn the distribution of real trajectories but are limited by the scarcity of large, real-world trajectory datasets needed for training. To tackle these challenges, we present AnonyTraj, a new trajectory publication mechanism that strikes a balance between privacy-preserving and data usability. Furthermore, AnonyTraj employs a fully convolutional neural network (FCN) that leverages map features to identify plausible paths given starting points and movement directions, significantly enhancing the accuracy of subsequent trajectory point sampling. By refining initial trajectories generated by a differentially private adaptive Markov model as a privacy-preserving post-processing step, AnonyTraj overcomes the issue of coarse-grained results and produces synthetic trajectories that are both privacy-preserving and highly usable. Notably, AnonyTraj improves data utility by at least 33% compared to current state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Research on Quality Anomaly Control Charts in Manufacturing Processes Based on Isolation Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of digitalization in the manufacturing industry, substantial amounts of data are generated during the production process. Many data-driven methods aim to quickly and accurately identify anomalies related to product quality or process states within massive highdimensional datasets. This study leverages binary partition trees to segment samples in high-dimensional datasets, demonstrating that anomalous samples require fewer partitions compared to ordinary samples. Using the Monte Carlo method, the average path length for the separation of anomalous samples is analyzed. Based on this analysis, a one-sided anomaly score control chart is developed to monitor anomalies in high-dimensional datasets. Application results demonstrate that the proposed method efficiently identifies anomalous samples in such datasets. These findings provide technical support for quality anomaly detection in multivariate manufacturing processes.

articleTitle: Facial Expression Recognition Using Segmentation Residual Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence and computer vision, facial expression recognition (FER) plays an increasingly important role in emotional communication. ResNet is a classical convolutional neural network that can be used for expression recognition. However, the performance of the model on FER2013 is not very good, because its ability to extract effective features is insufficient, and the key to the FER task is to extract effective features that help facial expression recognition. This paper proposes a Segmentation Residual Network (SRNet) network based on ResNet, which inherits ResNet ‘s residual module and ResNet ‘s similar architecture. The key of the network is to replace the Residual Block of ResNet with the Segmentation Residual Block (SRB) module designed in this paper. SRB is designed based on ResNet ‘s Residual Block and Attention U-net segmentation blocks. The network also integrates Spatial Transformer Network (STN) and Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks (SENet). Compared with the traditional ResNet, SRNet can extract effective features that are helpful for facial expression recognition and is more sensitive to the spatial transformation of facial features. The experimental results show that the SRNet model outperforms the state-of-the-art deep learning models in terms of sentiment classification accuracy on the FER2013 dataset.

articleTitle: A Novel Rotational Laser Vision Sensor for Industrial Robot Calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Industrial robots require high-precision calibration to perform tasks with accuracy and reliability in real-world environments. This study presents a novel rotational laser vision sensor designed to enhance the calibration accuracy of industrial robots. The key contribution of this paper is the high-precision modeling and calibration method for the proposed sensor, which effectively improves accuracy and repeatability. The sensor combines a rotating laser scanning mechanism with a monocular vision system, offering a compact design, high-efficiency area scanning, and laser resistance to interference. The sensor’s performance was evaluated through a series of experiments using a four-sphere calibration object for robot calibration. The Levenberg-Marquardt optimization algorithm was applied to identify the robot’s Denavit-Hartenberg (DH) parameters and external transformation matrices. The results show a substantial reduction in positioning errors, with the maximum error decreasing from 2.7468 mm to 0.1345 mm and the standard deviation from 0.5629 mm to 0.0296 mm after calibration.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction of Aerospace Quality Knowledge System and Proactive Services
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Aiming at the requirement of knowledge service in space quality management, this paper studies and proposes a solution based on knowledge graph and proactive service mechanism. Through the construction of structured knowledge graph, the effective organization and integration of complex quality management information is realized. This paper also introduces non-graph knowledge processing technology to extend the knowledge coverage. Scenario-based recommendation mechanism combines user portrait, context information and deep learning algorithm to achieve accurate knowledge push, including fuzzy matching and incomplete data information push methods. Through the case verification of space model quality problem zeroing, the system has achieved remarkable results in improving the speed of user knowledge acquisition, the relevance of recommended content and the efficiency of problem solving. The results show that this scheme has a good application prospect in the optimization of aerospace quality management process.

articleTitle: Intelligent Quality Control in Spare Parts Production: A Dual-Stage Hypothesis Testing Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the continuous development of intelligent manufacturing technologies, quality control issues in production processes have become increasingly complex, especially in large-scale production, where efficiently detecting and controlling defect rates has become a key challenge in ensuring product quality. This study proposes an engineering-oriented quality control optimization framework based on a dual-stage hypothesis test to evaluate whether the defect rate of spare parts meets the technical standards specified by suppliers. The framework first conducts a preliminary screening test on a small sample. If the results are inconclusive, a secondary validation test is performed on a larger sample, with acceptance or rejection thresholds set at specific confidence levels to strike a balance between accuracy and efficiency. Applied across key stages of production—including spare parts screening, product assembly, and returns handling—the framework demonstrates that selective testing of low-defectrate parts and optimized dismantling processes significantly enhance product quality stability. This framework not only provides strong support for quality management and improvement in engineering practice but also illustrates how the integration of statistical analysis and resource management methods can facilitate efficient quality control and risk prevention within the field of intelligent manufacturing, advancing the practical application of artificial intelligence technologies in production quality management.

articleTitle: Hybrid Opinion Dynamics Model Based on Community Relations and Neighbourhood Similarity
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Opinion dynamics models provide essential theoretical and practical tools for comprehending and optimizing information dissemination, policy design, and social phenomena. These models analyze the interactions between individuals to uncover and predict the mechanisms of group behavior and opinion formation. The existing hybrid opinion dynamics model, which combines SNDG and SNHK, is an innovative model that integrates the DeGroot model and the HK model. It also introduces dynamic network updating, incorporating a wider range of agent communication modes. However, this model overlooks the fact that the evolution of individual opinions in real life is often influenced by multiple factors. In this paper, we propose a new opinion dynamics model, NS-SNDG-HK, based on SNDG and SNHK. This model introduces a novel network updating strategy by considering the influence of opinions from the community and neighbors on individual opinions. We conduct experiments using several evaluation metrics on ER Random Networks and Scale-Free Networks to demonstrate that the community and neighbor relationships incorporated in the proposed NS-SNDG-HK model can significantly impact opinion evolution and network outcomes. Furthermore, the model accurately reveals and predicts group opinion propagation behavior, which aligns more closely with that observed in real social networks.

articleTitle: Spatial-Temporal Modeling of Urban Water Quality Using Gradient Boosting and H2O AutoML Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Considering the increasingly serious water pollution problem, this study focuses on the monitoring and prediction of urban water environment pollution. The study analyzed a set of daily water quality sample data released by the United States Geological Survey and proposed a series of urban water pollution prediction models that integrate temporal and spatial characteristics. Experimental results show that H2O AutoML achieved the lowest prediction error performance on the test set. The Gradient Boosting model significantly improves the prediction accuracy after adding the time dimension information. This study explored the significant effects of dissolved oxygen, water temperature and electrical conductivity on water quality indicators through feature association analysis, spatial distribution analysis and comparison of models in different dimensions, and proposed a method to incorporate time dimension information into the model to improve prediction accuracy. The research results provide an accurate early warning tool for urban water quality management and a scientific basis for optimizing resource allocation in water pollution management, which has important practical value and guiding significance.

articleTitle: A Visual SLAM Loop Closure Detection Method for Spraying Robots in Hilly Orchard
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: In the challenging environment of hilly orchards, vegetation occlusion, and variable lighting conditions lead to sparse and unevenly distributed visual features. Moreover, the extensive area covered by these orchards results in a vast volume of images that require efficient real-time processing. This paper introduces an enhanced loop closure detection method tailored for hilly orchard settings to address these issues. The proposed approach integrates adaptive threshold-adjusted uniform ORB feature extraction with CLBP features through the CBAM attention mechanism, creating a novel feature descriptor that emphasizes key information. Furthermore, it employs HNSW to expedite feature matching and adopts MAGSAC++ to refine geometric consistency verification. Experimental evaluations on a dataset of 2,347 images from hilly orchards demonstrate that our method achieves a precision rate of 75.75% with an average runtime of 8.73 seconds. Compared to the traditional ORB vocabulary model, this represents a significant improvement: the precision rate has increased by 21.73%, while the runtime has been reduced by $\mathbf{1 6. 9 2 \%}$. These enhancements underscore the method’s superior real-time performance and accuracy in detecting loop closures within hilly orchard environments, thereby providing robust technical support for the efficient operation of spraying robots in such settings.

articleTitle: An Improved Verification Method Based on Asynchronous Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: With the rapid development of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) technology, its applications have permeated various aspects of life and multiple industry sectors, significantly enhancing convenience. However, the large-scale deployment of HoT devices has also triggered numerous security issues, especially in enterprise-level applications. Although some current methods have alleviated these problems to a certain extent, they still face many challenges in practical applications. This paper proposes an improved solution based on asynchronous verification methods, integrating Risk Assessment Based on Security Baseline, Business Security Mechanisms, and Global Access Control List into the algorithms of the Verification Server. The aim of this method is to enhance internal traffic security by rejecting access from high-risk hosts, ensuring minimal API access authorization, and enforcing security policies, thereby avoiding the rapid depletion of resources at the Verification Server due to excessive malicious failed requests.

articleTitle: Type 1 Diabetes Blood Glucose Management Based on Fuzzy Logic and Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Developing a personalized insulin regimen for the treatment of Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) is a healthcare task with very high safety requirements. Compared to traditional control algorithms, current reinforcement learning-based methods for blood glucose control can increase the duration of blood glucose within the target range while reducing risks. However, they do not account for the uncertainties of factors affecting blood glucose levels, such as diet, age, weight, etc. These factors do not have a simple linear relationship with blood glucose changes. For example, consuming a certain amount of carbohydrates does not always immediately result in the same degree of blood glucose increase, and this variability is precisely the key to personalized insulin regimens. To address this issue, this work proposes a personalized insulin regimen based on fuzzy logic reasoning and reinforcement learning, namely the Fuzzy Rule-Based TD3-BC model (FRBTD3-BC). This regimen learns from real-world treatment data of T1D patients, uses membership functions to obtain the initial conditions and outcome categories of the data, and then calculates the weight of each rule based on confidence levels. Subsequently, a fuzzy rule base is obtained and embedded into the Actor module of the TD3-BC algorithm in the form of a fuzzy reasoning logic layer. By interacting with the FDA-approved UVA/Padova glucose kinetics simulator, the utility of FRBTD3BC in blood glucose control was studied in 30 virtual patients. The results show that the FRBTD3-BC model outperforms other comparable methods, with the TIR indicator increasing by 5.53 ± 0.64% compared to the original TD3-BC.

articleTitle: Study on Multi-Objective Optimization of Assembly Strategies for Building Constructions Based on BIM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: The construction industry is one of the key sectors for achieving carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals. Prefabricated buildings have gained significant attention due to their sustainability advantages in reducing the environmental impact of construction activities. During the assembly process of prefabricated components, different assembly rates have varying impacts on project carbon emissions and construction costs, necessitating a comprehensive balance of these factors. This study analyzes the calculation methods for carbon emissions during the construction phase and establishes a unified carbon emission calculation model applicable to both prefabricated and traditional cast-in-place construction methods. By integrating national coding standards with Revit’s built-in codes, a multi-objective optimization coding system for building components in BIM models is proposed. This system extends component attributes in BIM models to include carbon emission factors and cost information, forming a unified data foundation for optimizing assembly strategies. A binary differential evolution particle swarm optimization (BDEPSO) method is employed to establish a model for optimizing assembly strategies in prefabricated construction. A typical prefabricated substation project is used as a case study to validate the proposed method. Under specified assembly rate conditions, the project cost is reduced by approximately $\mathbf{1 2. 1 1 \%}$, and carbon emissions decrease by about 1%, demonstrating the method’s effectiveness and reliability. The results indicate that the proposed approach provides theoretical and practical support for the development of prefabricated buildings.

articleTitle: A Low-Light Imaging and Target Detection System Based on EBAPS
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Electron bombarded active pixel sensor (EBAPS), as a new type of digital low-light-level imaging device, can output clear images under both day and night conditions. Compared with visible light imaging and infrared imaging, its imaging system has other advantages such as miniaturization, low cost, and low power consumption, so which has become a research hotspot in the imaging field. Based on a Chinese domestic EBAPS low-light-level device, a fully low power design concept is adopted and RV1126 is selected as the core processor. Development of EBAPS device driving circuit, image processing and tracking circuit, and display circuit was completed. Meanwhile, an optical system that can be used day and night was constructed, and a miniaturized handheld imaging and target detection system was built. Experimental results show that the EBAPS day-night imaging system can achieve excellent imaging and detection performance under the illuminance conditions ranging from $1 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~lx}$ to $1 \times 10^{4} \mathrm{~lx}$.

articleTitle: Application of Key Technologies of Collaborative Networks in Intelligent Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: Intelligent manufacturing is an extension and expansion of the intelligent transformation of modern manufacturing industry, and collaborative networks are the infrastructure for promoting intelligent manufacturing services. In the traditional manufacturing network system, the design network is used to complete procurement and information modeling, while the production network is used to complete product and process modeling. These two networks are mutually isolated and cannot be connected, which affects the development of intelligent manufacturing. Collaborative networks not only have the function of integrating design networks and production networks, but also have the advantages of reducing development cycles and improving manufacturing efficiency. They can achieve the goal of collaborative work by relying on data generated throughout the design, manufacturing, and management process. In this context, this article conducts research by analyzing the research background, development history, information transmission problems, and security challenges of intelligent manufacturing collaborative networks, proposing a problem description and construction path for intelligent manufacturing collaborative networks, and presenting the design ideas of intelligent manufacturing collaborative networks based on SDN.

articleTitle: Intelligent SAR Target Recognition Technologies for High Dynamic Aerial Platforms : Methods, Challenges, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Manufacturing (AIIM)
abstract: SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) has gained widespread use in reconnaissance, monitoring, and other fields due to its unique advantage of all-weather, all-time imaging. With the evolving demands, intelligent SAR target recognition technology for high dynamic aerial platforms has become a research hotspot in this area. This paper provides a review from two perspectives: the traditional SAR ATR (Automatic Target Recognition) three-stage detection process and deep learning methods. First, the research progress in target recognition within traditional SAR ATR methods is reviewed, explaining their limitations in recognition accuracy. Next, the application of deep learning in SAR target detection and recognition is analyzed, emphasizing the advantages of deep learning technologies in automatic feature extraction and end-to-end training, we also demonstrate their potential to significantly improve recognition accuracy and overcome the limitations of traditional methods. Finally, the major challenges and future development directions of intelligent SAR target recognition technologies for high dynamic aerial platforms are discussed. This paper aims to provide comprehensive references and guidance for the research and application of airborne SAR target recognition technology.
